item.title: Is 16GB VRAM Enough for Serious Local LLM Work?
item.description: Size a 16GB local LLM setup around model weights, KV cache, and prompt processing. Compare Qwen3.8 27B memory budgets, GPU bandwidth, and ownership costs.
item.content:encoded: <p>16GB of dedicated GPU memory supports serious local LLM work when your model, context, and runtime fit together. Loading the weights proves only the first requirement. A useful setup also needs enough memory for your working conversation and enough speed to finish your task.</p> <p>Use Qwen3.8 27B as a worked example for budgeting a single-user coding or document workflow. Start with the context your task needs, then choose weights and runtime settings which fit the remaining memory. Hardware specifications and model sources were checked on October 7, 2026.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li>Reserve memory for context before choosing a quantization.</li> <li>Measure prompt processing separately from output speed.</li> <li>Disable unused vision support and test an 8-bit KV cache.</li> <li>Compare the exact GPU, backend, model file, and prompt length.</li> <li>Calculate ownership savings from your workload and provider bill.</li> </ul> <p>For the budgeting exercise, you need your runtime’s memory log, exact model filename, and a representative task. Allow about 20 minutes for setup and recording results, plus inference time. Difficulty is intermediate.</p> <h2 id="match-memory-to-work"> <a href="#match-memory-to-work" title="Match Memory to Work">Match Memory to Work</a> <a href="#match-memory-to-work" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Match Memory to Work">#</a> </h2> <p>16GB suits a workload whose weights, active context, and temporary allocations stay within available GPU memory. Your required context depends on the task. A short document summary and a coding agent reading dozens of files need different budgets.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Workload</th> <th>First sizing question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Short chat or drafting</td> <td>Does the model meet your quality target?</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Document analysis</td> <td>Do the source text and answer fit together?</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Coding agent</td> <td>How much context do files and tool results consume?</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Concurrent requests</td> <td>How much cache does each active session need?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>A configured window differs from an occupied window. A benchmark with a 64K limit and a short prompt does not measure generation after 55K tokens of conversation. Test near your expected session length before choosing hardware.</p> <h2 id="why-the-model-fits"> <a href="#why-the-model-fits" title="Why the Model Fits">Why the Model Fits</a> <a href="#why-the-model-fits" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Why the Model Fits">#</a> </h2> <p>Quantization stores weights with fewer bits. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Bartowski’s Qwen3.8 27B file table"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Bartowski’s Qwen3.8 27B file table</a> </span> lists Q4_K_M at 17.44 GB, already beyond a 16 GiB device’s approximately 17.18 billion bytes before runtime memory.</p> <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="ISTA-DASLab’s GSQ-RCO model card"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >ISTA-DASLab’s GSQ-RCO model card</a> </span> lists IQ3_S at 11.8 GB. Its method assigns different precision to different tensors within a size budget. The optional MTP version adds about 0.35 GB, while the vision projector adds about 0.9 GB.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Published benchmark</th> <th>BF16 / IQ3_S score</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>AIME25</td> <td>100.00 / 100.00</td> </tr> <tr> <td>LiveCodeBench v6</td> <td>85.71 / 85.71</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPQA-Diamond</td> <td>89.90 / 89.39</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The lab calls this operating point “task-lossless.” These selected results support a narrow comparison. They do not prove identical answers, equal long-context retrieval, or equal reliability across your coding tasks. Test the compressed model against your own acceptance criteria.</p> <h2 id="count-the-cache"> <a href="#count-the-cache" title="Count the Cache">Count the Cache</a> <a href="#count-the-cache" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Count the Cache">#</a> </h2> <p>The KV cache stores attention keys and values for tokens already processed. Your prompt, tool output, and generated answers consume context. Some runtimes allocate cache capacity at startup, so displayed memory need not grow with every message.</p> <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Qwen’s configuration"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/main/config.json"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/main/config.json" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Qwen’s configuration</a> </span> specifies 64 layers, with full attention every fourth layer, four KV heads, and a head dimension of 256. For those 16 full-attention layers, the calculated FP16 cache cost is:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>16 layers × 4 KV heads × 256 elements × 2 (K and V) × 2 bytes </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>= 65,536 bytes per token </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>= 64 KiB per token </span></span></code></pre></div><p>This calculation excludes recurrent state, alignment, temporary buffers, and speculative decoding allocations. Other architectures need different calculations.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Occupied tokens</th> <th>FP16 full-attention cache</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>32,768</td> <td>2 GiB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>65,536</td> <td>4 GiB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>131,072</td> <td>8 GiB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>262,144</td> <td>16 GiB</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Here, KiB and GiB use powers of 1024. Model download sizes use decimal GB. Mixing the units distorts the remaining budget.</p> <h2 id="budget-your-available-context"> <a href="#budget-your-available-context" title="Budget Your Available Context">Budget Your Available Context</a> <a href="#budget-your-available-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Budget Your Available Context">#</a> </h2> <p>Two settings free memory for longer text sessions: remove an unused vision projector and reduce cache precision. Calculate their effect against your loaded model and runtime allocations.</p> <p>Use this worked example, with every allocation expressed in decimal GB. The 1.0 GB reserve below is a planning assumption, not a universal runtime default.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Allocation</th> <th>Vision on / vision off</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Physical 16 GiB capacity</td> <td>17.180 / 17.180 GB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Model weights</td> <td>11.800 / 11.800 GB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Optional MTP head</td> <td>0.350 / 0.350 GB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Vision projector estimate</td> <td>0.930 / 0 GB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Assumed other allocations</td> <td>1.000 / 1.000 GB</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Left for growing cache</td> <td>3.100 / 4.030 GB</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>At 65,536 bytes per token, 3.100 GB holds about 47,300 tokens. With vision disabled, ideal 8-bit storage would use 32,768 bytes per token and hold about 123,000 tokens.</p> <p>Real q8_0 storage includes block scales. At 34 bytes per 32 values, this example needs about 34,816 bytes per token, reducing the estimate to roughly 115,700. Additional allocations reduce the result further. Around 110K is therefore a plausible planning result under these assumptions, not a guaranteed setting.</p> <p>The remaining context must cover both input and output. With a 65,536-token window, an illustrative 30,000-token initial prompt and an 8,192-token output allowance leave 27,344 tokens for files, tool results, and conversation. The initial prompt budget is an example. Measure your own tools and instructions.</p> <h2 id="settings-worth-testing"> <a href="#settings-worth-testing" title="Settings Worth Testing">Settings Worth Testing</a> <a href="#settings-worth-testing" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Settings Worth Testing">#</a> </h2> <p>The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="llama.cpp server documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/server"> <a href="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/server" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >llama.cpp server documentation</a> </span> documents separate key and value cache types, automatic projector loading, and parallel slots. For a text-only workload, test vision disabled, q8_0 for both cache types, and one slot. Use a modest context first.</p> <p>Record the resulting allocations before increasing context. Cache quantization needs support from your selected architecture and backend. Test answer quality after changing precision. Keep a working configuration for comparison.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/weights-cache-runtime-budget.webp", "caption": "Illustration of a graphics card beside blue, purple, and orange blocks representing separate memory allocations", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.391811127 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.357425816", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.391811127 +0000 UTC m=+546.357425816"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/weights-cache-runtime-budget.webp" alt="Illustration of a graphics card beside blue, purple, and orange blocks representing separate memory allocations"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Blue represents weights, purple represents context cache, and orange represents runtime allocations. Sizes are illustrative</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="why-speeds-differ"> <a href="#why-speeds-differ" title="Why Speeds Differ">Why Speeds Differ</a> <a href="#why-speeds-differ" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Why Speeds Differ">#</a> </h2> <p>A 16GB label describes capacity. Throughput also depends on memory bandwidth, compute kernels, active context, offload, batching, and speculative decoding.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Cause</th> <th>What to inspect</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>CPU or RAM offload</td> <td>Loaded layer placement and cache location</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Long context</td> <td>Occupied tokens during the measurement</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Backend differences</td> <td>Runtime commit, driver, and kernel path</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Speculative decoding</td> <td>Accepted drafts and extra allocations</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>For a dense model generating one token at a time, memory bandwidth divided by resident weight bytes gives a rough bandwidth-only estimate. At 448 GB/s and 11.8 GB of weights, the quotient is about 38 tokens per second. Cache reads and computation add work, while speculative decoding and batching change the assumptions.</p> <p>Do not treat this quotient as a universal upper bound. A higher reported output rate does not automatically invalidate a benchmark. Check whether one target-model pass accepted multiple draft tokens.</p> <p>Multi-token prediction, or MTP, needs a compatible model and runtime. Compare enabled and disabled runs at both short and long occupied context. Extra weights and draft state consume memory, but no universal rule requires disabling MTP after 32K tokens.</p> <h2 id="measure-the-first-reply"> <a href="#measure-the-first-reply" title="Measure the First Reply">Measure the First Reply</a> <a href="#measure-the-first-reply" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Measure the First Reply">#</a> </h2> <p>Prefill processes the prompt before generation. Decode produces the answer. A fast decode result hides a slow first response when a task begins with a large uncached prompt.</p> <p>Divide uncached prompt tokens by measured prefill throughput to estimate prompt-processing time. For a fresh 30,000-token prompt, two illustrative rates produce these waits:</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Example prompt rate</th> <th>Calculated processing time</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>750 tokens/s</td> <td>40 seconds</td> </tr> <tr> <td>150 tokens/s</td> <td>200 seconds</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>These examples describe processing time, excluding model loading and request overhead. Prompt length, batch size, model format, and backend affect your measured rate.</p> <p>Measure a cold request and a continuation with a reusable prefix separately. Prefix reuse avoids processing some repeated input. Record time to first token alongside decode rate and total task duration.</p> <h2 id="compare-complete-gpu-setups"> <a href="#compare-complete-gpu-setups" title="Compare Complete GPU Setups">Compare Complete GPU Setups</a> <a href="#compare-complete-gpu-setups" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare Complete GPU Setups">#</a> </h2> <p>Compare purchase price, usable memory, bandwidth, and the software path together. A lower-priced card loses its advantage if your workload requires unsupported features or takes longer than your latency target.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>16GB desktop card</th> <th>Memory bandwidth</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>RX 9060 XT</td> <td>320 GB/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td>RTX 5060 Ti</td> <td>448 GB/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td>RX 9070</td> <td>640 GB/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td>RX 9070 XT</td> <td>640 GB/s</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>AMD’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="RX 9070 specifications"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.amd.com/en/products/graphics/desktops/radeon/9000-series/amd-radeon-rx-9070.html"> <a href="https://www.amd.com/en/products/graphics/desktops/radeon/9000-series/amd-radeon-rx-9070.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >RX 9070 specifications</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="RX 9070 XT specifications"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.amd.com/en/products/graphics/desktops/radeon/9000-series/amd-radeon-rx-9070xt.html"> <a href="https://www.amd.com/en/products/graphics/desktops/radeon/9000-series/amd-radeon-rx-9070xt.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >RX 9070 XT specifications</a> </span> confirm their 16GB capacity and up-to-640 GB/s bandwidth. The 640-to-448 comparison yields about 43% more theoretical bandwidth. A 43% inference improvement does not follow from those specifications.</p> <p>Choose from benchmarks using your intended model and backend. For short prompts and sustained generation, decode performance deserves more weight. For repository analysis, prioritize cold prefill, long-context speed, and successful task completion. Check available software before buying either vendor.</p> <h2 id="macs-and-laptop-labels"> <a href="#macs-and-laptop-labels" title="Macs and Laptop Labels">Macs and Laptop Labels</a> <a href="#macs-and-laptop-labels" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Macs and Laptop Labels">#</a> </h2> <p>A 16GB Apple silicon Mac shares memory among the CPU, GPU, operating system, and applications. A discrete 16GB GPU has dedicated video memory alongside system RAM. These capacities do not describe equivalent model budgets.</p> <p>Apple exposes a <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="recommended GPU working-set size"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtldevice/recommendedmaxworkingsetsize"> <a href="https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtldevice/recommendedmaxworkingsetsize" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >recommended GPU working-set size</a> </span> . Inspect your runtime’s reported allowance and system memory pressure. Leave room for macOS and your other applications instead of budgeting the entire shared pool for inference.</p> <p>For laptops, check the manufacturer’s exact SKU, dedicated memory, GPU power limit, and cooling. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="NVIDIA’s RTX 5060 family page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/graphics-cards/50-series/rtx-5060-family/"> <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/graphics-cards/50-series/rtx-5060-family/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >NVIDIA’s RTX 5060 family page</a> </span> lists desktop RTX 5060 Ti memory variants. A family name alone does not establish 16GB, and desktop results do not establish laptop throughput.</p> <h2 id="does-ownership-pay"> <a href="#does-ownership-pay" title="Does Ownership Pay?">Does Ownership Pay?</a> <a href="#does-ownership-pay" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Does Ownership Pay?">#</a> </h2> <p>Ownership pays financially when avoided hosting charges exceed operating costs and recover the hardware purchase. Start with an output-only example: a $789 card, 35 output tokens/s, 180W during generation, $0.18/kWh electricity, and $2.95 per million hosted output tokens. These are illustrative inputs. Replace them with your purchase quote, measured power, electricity rate, and provider pricing.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Hours per million output tokens = 1,000,000 ÷ 35 ÷ 3,600 = 7.94 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Electricity per million = 7.94 × 0.180 kW × $0.18/kWh = $0.257 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Savings per million = $2.95 - $0.257 = $2.693 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Break-even output = $789 ÷ $2.693 = 293 million tokens </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Continuous generation time = 293 × 7.94 ÷ 24 = about 97 days </span></span></code></pre></div><p>At eight hours of uninterrupted generation per day, the same calculation takes about 291 days. Eight hours with an assistant open is different from eight hours generating tokens.</p> <p>At a hosted output price of $0.16 per million, local electricity in this scenario already costs more than hosting. There is no positive output-only break-even point under these assumptions.</p> <p>Use the selected provider’s current <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenRouter model pricing"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://openrouter.ai/qwen/qwen3.8-27b"> <a href="https://openrouter.ai/qwen/qwen3.8-27b" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >OpenRouter model pricing</a> </span> , including input and cached-input charges. Measure whole-system energy, including prefill. Add upgrades, idle energy, maintenance, and expected resale value. Compare accepted work, since retries and quality differences change cost per task.</p> <h2 id="when-to-add-memory"> <a href="#when-to-add-memory" title="When to Add Memory">When to Add Memory</a> <a href="#when-to-add-memory" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="When to Add Memory">#</a> </h2> <p>Move beyond 16GB when your measured workload exceeds available context at acceptable quality and latency. Daily long agent sessions, concurrent requests, or higher-precision weights make larger capacity useful.</p> <p>Two 16GB cards require explicit runtime support. They do not become one transparent 32GB allocation. Each device needs buffers, and communication uses the host’s interconnect.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Split strategy</th> <th>Main tradeoff</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Layer split</td> <td>Different layers occupy different devices</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Tensor or row split</td> <td>Work within layers adds communication</td> </tr> <tr> <td>CPU plus GPU</td> <td>More capacity with a different latency profile</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>A second card deserves consideration when your motherboard, power supply, cooling, and backend already support the plan. Compare complete system cost with a larger single GPU. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="32GB Qwen hardware guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/32gb-vram-qwen-27b-hardware-guide/"> <a href="/articles/32gb-vram-qwen-27b-hardware-guide/" rel="follow me" >32GB Qwen hardware guide</a> </span> covers those alternatives.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-next-steps"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">Troubleshooting and Next Steps</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>If loading fails, lower context and inspect allocations. If speed falls during a session, check occupied context and CPU offload. If the first response stalls, measure cold prefill. If tool use breaks after compression, compare the same task with a higher-precision model.</p> <p>Save one repeatable test containing your normal instructions, files, and tool outputs. Record model revision, runtime version, cache precision, occupied context, peak memory, first-token latency, decode speed, and whether the task passed. Repeat near your longest expected session.</p> <p>Use the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="local model and context guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/"> <a href="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/" rel="follow me" >local model and context guide</a> </span> to compare smaller alternatives. Choose the smallest model meeting your quality requirements, then reserve enough memory for the complete task. Under those conditions, 16GB is a useful workstation target.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: 10 Claude Code Plugins, Skills, and MCP Tools: A Practical Guide
item.description: Choose Claude Code extensions for planning, code review, knowledge management, design, and automation. Compare ten tools, dependencies, and practical checks.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Choose a Claude Code extension around a specific failure in your workflow.</strong> Unclear requirements need a planning conversation. Missed defects need review and tests. Repeated research needs traceable sources. Installing more tools only helps when their responsibilities are clear.</p> <p>This guide compares <strong>ten projects</strong> across those jobs, with setup examples and a worked evaluation exercise. The analysis draws on current project documentation and the supplied Chase AI video. Recommendations are editorial judgments, not hands-on performance measurements or evidence of a tenfold productivity increase.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Choose by output:</strong> a reviewed plan, a code map, and a generated image require different tools.</li> <li><strong>Separate installation layers:</strong> instructions, executable programs, plugins, and service connections have different dependencies.</li> <li><strong>Check current names:</strong> Graphify and grill-me-codex now have different canonical repository locations.</li> <li><strong>Verify beyond agreement:</strong> two models accepting a plan does not establish correct implementation.</li> <li><strong>Measure accepted work:</strong> include setup, service usage, failed attempts, and human corrections.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-start"> <a href="#before-you-start" title="Before You Start">Before You Start</a> <a href="#before-you-start" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Start">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> a working Claude Code installation, a disposable project or branch, and permission to use the selected external services. CLI examples assume a terminal and the named package manager. Cloud integrations require their own accounts and authentication.</p> <p><strong>Estimated time:</strong> 15 minutes to read, then allow 30 to 60 minutes for one bounded trial. <strong>Difficulty:</strong> intermediate for CLI setup and service integration. Reading instruction skills requires less setup.</p> <p><strong>Documentation checked October 6, 2026.</strong> Commands and access rules reflect the linked sources. Recheck your installed version before following an older tutorial. This article focuses on extensions used from Claude Code, with host differences called out where relevant.</p> <h2 id="know-the-extension-type"> <a href="#know-the-extension-type" title="Know the Extension Type">Know the Extension Type</a> <a href="#know-the-extension-type" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Know the Extension Type">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Type</th> <th>Role</th> <th>Example</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Instruction file</strong></td> <td>Sets persistent project expectations</td> <td>CLAUDE.md</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Skill</strong></td> <td>Supplies a procedure for a selected task</td> <td>grill-me</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Plugin</strong></td> <td>Packages registered commands and integrations</td> <td>Codex plugin</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>CLI</strong></td> <td>Executes commands from a terminal</td> <td>Graphify</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>MCP server</strong></td> <td>Exposes callable tools to an agent client</td> <td>n8n instance integration</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Model Context Protocol (MCP)</strong> connects an agent application to tools and data exposed by a server. A command-line interface, or <strong>CLI</strong>, runs executable commands. A skill often teaches the agent how to use either interface, but its presence does not establish a working connection.</p> <p><strong>Start with the missing capability.</strong> If your agent already has repository search, a new search procedure needs an observable benefit. If the agent lacks access to an automation platform, a prose instruction file alone will not supply authenticated access. Compare accepted results, including your review effort and failed attempts.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Interpretation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Faster answer, failed tests</strong></td> <td>Lower response time without task completion</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Longer run, fewer corrections</strong></td> <td>Possible benefit in total delivery effort</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Two agreeing reviewers</strong></td> <td>Agreement requiring independent verification</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Lower agent usage, new service charges</strong></td> <td>Cost moved across providers</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Create a retained decision record.</strong> Name the problem, selected tool, observed benefit, unresolved issue, and conditions for another trial. Keep a tool when its contribution survives this check. A large installed collection does not require a large active workflow.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Symptom</th> <th>Check next</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Skill exists but command fails</strong></td> <td>Executable installation, PATH, and required sidecar files</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Old tutorial names missing commands</strong></td> <td>Installed version and canonical upstream instructions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Graph misses recent changes</strong></td> <td>Graph freshness and separate document refresh</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Reviewer repeats resolved objections</strong></td> <td>Exact plan revision, evidence, and review budget</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Notebook authentication fails</strong></td> <td>Auth diagnostic, session validity, and upstream issues</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>n8n connection lacks expected operations</strong></td> <td>Deployed version, exposure settings, and granted permissions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Design looks better but works worse</strong></td> <td>Original acceptance criteria and interaction checks</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Check installation layers in order:</strong> files present, host discovery, dependencies ready, authentication working, and representative task verified. A successful installer establishes only part of this chain.</p> <p><strong>Inspect overlapping skills before adding another copy.</strong> Requirements interviews, planning suites, design tools, and review packages sometimes express competing defaults. Select one primary procedure for the job, then add supporting tools for named contributions. Preserve repository policy and the user’s requested scope.</p> <h2 id="video-walkthrough"> <a href="#video-walkthrough" title="Video Walkthrough">Video Walkthrough</a> <a href="#video-walkthrough" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Video Walkthrough">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); item.title: 9 AI Agent Skill Projects for Research, Design, and Development
item.description: Compare nine agent skill projects by workflow, host support, dependencies, and cost. Learn how to install, inspect, and test the skills you need.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Install an agent skill to improve a repeatable task.</strong> Researching current discussions, reviewing interface design, and rendering a video involve different procedures and dependencies. A useful skill supplies the missing instructions, reference material, or scripts for one of those jobs.</p> <p><strong>Nine projects deserve consideration:</strong> last30days, Humanizer, Impeccable, Superpowers, gstack, Claude Video, Remotion, HyperFrames, and NVIDIA SkillSpector. Some are instruction bundles, some include executable tools, and some are frameworks with companion skills. This guide compares their documented roles and provides a practical way to select, install, and evaluate them.</p> <p><strong>Documentation snapshot: October 6, 2026.</strong> Recommendations reflect project documentation and source inspection, not a comparative benchmark of output quality. Free installation does not establish free inference, rendering, data access, or commercial use.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Start with a recurring job:</strong> choose a skill with a clear output and acceptance check.</li> <li><strong>Separate skills from runtimes:</strong> installing instructions does not install every required executable.</li> <li><strong>Check the host:</strong> a working Claude Code integration does not establish identical Codex or Cowork behavior.</li> <li><strong>Inspect permissions and dependencies:</strong> package commands, hooks, external services, and credentials need separate attention.</li> <li><strong>Customize after testing:</strong> keep project policy authoritative and preserve a record of upstream versions.</li> </ul> <h2 id="choose-by-deliverable"> <a href="#choose-by-deliverable" title="Choose by Deliverable">Choose by Deliverable</a> <a href="#choose-by-deliverable" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose by Deliverable">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Required output</th> <th>Project to evaluate</th> <th>First check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Current discussion brief</strong></td> <td>last30days</td> <td>Which sources returned usable evidence?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Edited prose</strong></td> <td>Humanizer</td> <td>Did meaning and attribution survive?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Improved interface</strong></td> <td>Impeccable</td> <td>Does the revised interaction work?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Planned and tested change</strong></td> <td>Superpowers</td> <td>Does the process match task complexity?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Review and QA workflow</strong></td> <td>gstack</td> <td>Which features work on your agent host?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Video observations</strong></td> <td>Claude Video / Watch</td> <td>Are claims supported by frames or audio?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>React video composition</strong></td> <td>Remotion skills</td> <td>Does the exported video match the preview?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>HTML video composition</strong></td> <td>HyperFrames skills</td> <td>Is animation deterministic when seeking?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Skill inspection report</strong></td> <td>SkillSpector</td> <td>Was analysis complete, and what was flagged?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>A skill differs from an agent harness.</strong> A skill supplies task-specific guidance and sometimes scripts. The harness decides how the agent loads instructions, calls tools, and enforces permissions. Our <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="agent-harness comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/best-ai-agent-harnesses/"> <a href="/articles/best-ai-agent-harnesses/" rel="follow me" >agent-harness comparison</a> </span> covers those surrounding systems.</p> <p><strong>A skill folder is also not a plugin installation.</strong> Plugins sometimes register hooks or additional tools which a manual folder copy omits. Read the instructions for your particular host and installation mode before assuming equivalent behavior.</p> <h2 id="research-and-writing"> <a href="#research-and-writing" title="Research and Writing">Research and Writing</a> <a href="#research-and-writing" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Research and Writing">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="last30days"> <a href="#last30days" title="last30days">last30days</a> <a href="#last30days" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="last30days">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use last30days for recent discussion research.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="project"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill"> <a href="https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >project</a> </span> combines sources such as Reddit, Hacker News, YouTube, X, and the web. Available coverage depends on the selected sources, installed tools, authentication, and provider access. Its preflight mode describes planned access and writes without starting research.</p> <p><strong>Ask for an evidence trail.</strong> A useful result includes dates, links, recurring complaints, and disagreements. An unavailable source should appear as a coverage gap. Engagement counts describe activity among collected posts, not a representative survey of every user.</p> <p><strong>Illustrative task:</strong> investigate recurring installation failures for a library released recently. Group reports by version and operating system, then verify proposed fixes against the library’s issue tracker or documentation. Avoid treating a popular workaround as an upstream-supported solution.</p> <h3 id="humanizer"> <a href="#humanizer" title="Humanizer">Humanizer</a> <a href="#humanizer" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Humanizer">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use Humanizer as an editing pass.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="skill"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/blader/humanizer"> <a href="https://github.com/blader/humanizer" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >skill</a> </span> targets repetitive contrasts, staged introductions, inflated claims, and other writing habits. It accepts voice samples and aims to preserve the underlying meaning.</p> <p><strong>Supply the constraints alongside the draft.</strong> Identify the audience, facts which must remain, and citations which must stay attached. After editing, compare the factual claims with the original. Better rhythm is useful, but it does not validate an unsupported statistic.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Writing check</th> <th>Passing result</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Meaning</strong></td> <td>Same claims, qualifications, and scope</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Sources</strong></td> <td>Attribution remains near borrowed findings</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Voice</strong></td> <td>Matches the intended reader and supplied examples</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Originality</strong></td> <td>Adds independent reasoning instead of disguising copied prose</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Use these projects at different stages.</strong> last30days gathers material for investigation. Humanizer edits expression. Neither replaces source verification or independent authorship.</p> <h2 id="interface-and-development-work"> <a href="#interface-and-development-work" title="Interface and Development Work">Interface and Development Work</a> <a href="#interface-and-development-work" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Interface and Development Work">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="impeccable"> <a href="#impeccable" title="Impeccable">Impeccable</a> <a href="#impeccable" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Impeccable">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use Impeccable for focused design work.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="website"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://impeccable.style/"> <a href="https://impeccable.style/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >website</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="repository"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable"> <a href="https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >repository</a> </span> document a design workflow covering critique, typography, layout, clarity, motion, and polish. Begin with a specific user problem rather than asking for a vaguely more impressive page.</p> <p><strong>An illustrative brief:</strong> make a subscription settings page easier to scan without hiding cancellation or changing keyboard navigation. Request a critique first, then implement the selected changes. Check mobile layout, focus order, contrast, and completion of the original task afterward.</p> <p><strong>Installation mode matters.</strong> The current Codex instructions distinguish the skill from a project-local design hook. Hook trust requires its own approval in Codex. A copied skill folder does not establish an active hook.</p> <h3 id="superpowers"> <a href="#superpowers" title="Superpowers">Superpowers</a> <a href="#superpowers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Superpowers">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use Superpowers for a structured development process.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="repository"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/obra/superpowers"> <a href="https://github.com/obra/superpowers" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >repository</a> </span> packages workflows for brainstorming, planning, testing, debugging, and review. It also documents host-specific plugin installation, including Codex.</p> <p><strong>Match the process to the assignment.</strong> A feature spanning data storage, UI, and tests benefits from an explicit plan. A spelling correction needs much less ceremony. Define the authorized scope so a general development workflow does not expand a small request into adjacent work.</p> <p><strong>Project instructions still apply.</strong> A skill’s preferred testing method, worktree approach, or delegation pattern must fit the repository and the user’s request. Installing a methodology does not authorize every action described within it.</p> <h3 id="gstack"> <a href="#gstack" title="gstack">gstack</a> <a href="#gstack" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="gstack">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use gstack for a broader engineering workflow with executable tooling.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/garrytan/gstack"> <a href="https://github.com/garrytan/gstack" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >documentation</a> </span> includes planning, review, browser QA, investigation, and release-oriented skills. Installation builds supporting tools rather than merely copying prose.</p> <p><strong>Codex support is currently experimental.</strong> The project distinguishes Claude Code’s hook-enforced safety features from advisory behavior on Codex. Do not assume a similarly named command supplies identical enforcement across hosts.</p> <p><strong>My selection rule:</strong> trial Superpowers when the missing piece is a repeatable development process. Trial gstack when its specific review or browser tools solve a current need. If both are installed, choose one primary workflow per task and invoke the other for a named contribution.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Development problem</th> <th>Useful evaluation task</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Unclear scope</strong></td> <td>Produce a bounded plan with acceptance criteria</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Fragile implementation</strong></td> <td>Fix a seeded regression and preserve existing behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Broken interaction</strong></td> <td>Reproduce a browser failure and retain evidence</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Conflicting workflows</strong></td> <td>Confirm only the selected process directs the task</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="video-evidence-and-production"> <a href="#video-evidence-and-production" title="Video Evidence and Production">Video Evidence and Production</a> <a href="#video-evidence-and-production" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Video Evidence and Production">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="claude-video--watch"> <a href="#claude-video--watch" title="Claude Video / Watch">Claude Video / Watch</a> <a href="#claude-video--watch" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Claude Video / Watch">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use Claude Video to collect evidence from a video.</strong> Despite the repository name, its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch skill"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/bradautomates/claude-video"> <a href="https://github.com/bradautomates/claude-video" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch skill</a> </span> supports local agents including Codex. Its local route uses downloads, sampled frames, and captions or transcription. A separate Gemini route sends video for model analysis when configured.</p> <p><strong>Check current host support.</strong> The README lists Claude Chat and Cowork as unsupported. Local execution requires media tools such as FFmpeg and yt-dlp, and individual websites still impose access limits.</p> <p><strong>Keep visual and audio claims separate.</strong> A transcript supports spoken words. Frames support visible details at sampled times. Neither establishes an unseen event between samples. Ask for timestamps and unresolved observations rather than an unqualified claim to have understood the entire recording.</p> <h3 id="remotion"> <a href="#remotion" title="Remotion">Remotion</a> <a href="#remotion" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Remotion">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use Remotion for video compositions written in React.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="framework repository"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/remotion-dev/remotion"> <a href="https://github.com/remotion-dev/remotion" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >framework repository</a> </span> points to a separate <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="agent-skills collection"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/skills"> <a href="https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/skills" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >agent-skills collection</a> </span> . The collection covers project creation, markup, maps, captions, Studio, and rendering. Installing the collection does not create a video project or install all project dependencies.</p> <p><strong>Check licensing independently of the skill download.</strong> Remotion’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="pricing page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license/pricing"> <a href="https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license/pricing" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >pricing page</a> </span> lists a free license for individuals and companies of up to three people, with company licensing for larger organizations and specified collaborations. Review the current terms for your use case.</p> <h3 id="hyperframes"> <a href="#hyperframes" title="HyperFrames">HyperFrames</a> <a href="#hyperframes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="HyperFrames">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Use HyperFrames for HTML-based video composition.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="repository"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes"> <a href="https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >repository</a> </span> describes rendering HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animation into MP4. The published skills guide composition, preview, validation, and rendering.</p> <p><strong>Begin with its documented core set.</strong> The current installation guidance distinguishes core skills from the larger published collection and repository-internal skills. An indiscriminate install of every folder adds unrelated instructions and makes maintenance harder.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Video workflow</th> <th>Important acceptance check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Watch</strong></td> <td>Timestamped observations agree with inspected media</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Remotion</strong></td> <td>Final export preserves timing, fonts, audio, and layout</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>HyperFrames</strong></td> <td>Seeking to a frame produces the intended visual state</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Choose through a controlled sample.</strong> Give Remotion and HyperFrames the same brief, assets, duration, and output dimensions. For example, animate a three-step maintenance procedure with captions and one diagram. Compare the exported files, editing effort, and render failures. A single attractive demo does not establish a general winner.</p> <h2 id="inspect-with-skillspector"> <a href="#inspect-with-skillspector" title="Inspect With SkillSpector">Inspect With SkillSpector</a> <a href="#inspect-with-skillspector" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect With SkillSpector">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>skillspector scan ./downloaded-skill --no-llm --format json --output report.json </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>NVIDIA SkillSpector is a scanner, not a video or writing skill.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="project"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector"> <a href="https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >project</a> </span> documents static checks and optional model-assisted analysis for agent skill packages. The command above assumes the CLI is already installed and scans a local folder without executing the target skill.</p> <p><strong>Read the findings and coverage together.</strong> Inspect flagged files and surrounding code, then record which checks completed. An incomplete scan should not become a clean verdict. A keyword hit also needs context: a provider’s documented public map token differs from code collecting unrelated credentials.</p> <p><strong>Static-only does not mean fully offline.</strong> According to the project, dependency names and versions still go to OSV for vulnerability lookup with <strong><code>--no-llm</code></strong>. Enabling model analysis additionally sends eligible file contents to the configured provider. Choose the mode appropriate for the material under review.</p> <p><strong>Use the report as evidence for a decision.</strong> Explain whether each finding is necessary for the stated task, which data leaves the machine, and what authority the runtime grants. A low score is not proof of safety, and reputation does not resolve an unexplained finding.</p> <h2 id="install-the-correct-package"> <a href="#install-the-correct-package" title="Install the Correct Package">Install the Correct Package</a> <a href="#install-the-correct-package" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Install the Correct Package">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Identify the canonical skill distribution first.</strong> The Remotion framework and its skills live in different repositories. Claude Video exposes a skill named Watch. SkillSpector is installed as a CLI, with agent integration handled separately. Those distinctions explain why cloning a project is not always enough.</p> <p><strong>Example commands below come from the projects’ current installation documentation.</strong> Run only the command for the selected project. The package runner downloads and executes installer code, so inspect the upstream project and choose your installation scope before running it.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Humanizer: user-wide Codex installation</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>npx skills add blader/humanizer --global --agent codex </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># last30days: user-wide Codex installation</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g -a codex </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Remotion: official skill collection, not the framework repository</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>npx skills add remotion-dev/skills </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The third command opens the installer workflow.</strong> Select the intended agent and scope rather than assuming its defaults match the explicitly scoped commands above. Plugin installers and standalone folder installs also have different update mechanisms.</p> <p><strong>Preserve existing installations.</strong> Before replacing a skill, check its version, local changes, and manager. Avoid keeping multiple competing copies in user, project, and plugin locations unless the host documents how it resolves them.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Installation state</th> <th>What it establishes</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Files present</strong></td> <td>Instructions and referenced assets exist</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Host discovers skill</strong></td> <td>The agent recognizes its name and description</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Dependencies ready</strong></td> <td>Required executables and packages are available</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Task verified</strong></td> <td>A representative result passes independent checks</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Verify each stage in order.</strong> A successful folder copy is an installation check, not evidence of a working browser, download, transcription, or render. Keep optional provider setup separate from the basic installation and avoid storing credentials in skill files.</p> <h2 id="test-before-customizing"> <a href="#test-before-customizing" title="Test Before Customizing">Test Before Customizing</a> <a href="#test-before-customizing" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Test Before Customizing">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use one saved task as a baseline.</strong> Run it without the new skill, then with the skill while holding the model, input, tools, and acceptance criteria steady where possible. Record failures and human corrections alongside the final result.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Illustrative evaluation record, not a skill configuration schema</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">job</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"review a settings page"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">input</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"same source revision and test data"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">variants</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"agent without the selected skill"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"same agent with the selected skill"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">acceptance</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"required actions remain visible"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"keyboard navigation works"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"mobile layout remains usable"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">record</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"skill source and revision"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"model and enabled tools"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"completed checks and retained evidence"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"elapsed time and manual corrections"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">"external service usage"</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Customize the repeated failure, not the entire package.</strong> If research summaries lose conflicting evidence, add a requirement to preserve dissenting sources. If a design pass changes established colors, point it to the design tokens. If video captions overflow, add an export-resolution check.</p> <p><strong>Keep local additions traceable.</strong> Record the upstream revision, your changes, and the task which motivated them. Updates deserve another trial because new triggers, scripts, or dependencies change the workflow you previously evaluated.</p> <p><strong>Watch for overlapping instructions.</strong> Development suites, design skills, and prose editors all express preferences. Repository rules and the user’s current request should resolve conflicts. A style skill should not strip required accessibility labels, remove citations, or rewrite technical terms merely to vary the wording.</p> <h2 id="build-a-useful-library"> <a href="#build-a-useful-library" title="Build a Useful Library">Build a Useful Library</a> <a href="#build-a-useful-library" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build a Useful Library">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start with the job you repeat most often.</strong> A writer might trial last30days and Humanizer. A frontend developer might begin with Impeccable and one development workflow. A video producer should choose a production framework and add Watch when source-video analysis is part of the work.</p> <p><strong>Budget for operation separately from installation.</strong> Account for model calls, optional search providers, transcription, media generation, rendering infrastructure, and applicable licenses. A free repository answers only part of the cost question.</p> <p><strong>Before your first trial:</strong> prepare approved model access, a disposable project or sample input, and written acceptance criteria. Basic instruction skills are accessible to beginners. Browser tooling, media dependencies, and cloud rendering require more setup. Allow an initial hour for a bounded trial, then repeat it with representative inputs before making the workflow routine.</p> <p><strong>Keep skills with demonstrated value.</strong> Retain the ones which reduce missed steps or review effort, and remove duplicates which introduce conflicting behavior. Revisit their host compatibility and dependencies when your agent environment changes.</p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if
