item.title: Best AI Agent Harnesses in 2026: Choose by Workflow
item.description: Compare Deep Agents, Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Pydantic AI, Pi, and LangGraph by tool execution, memory, recovery, and integration effort.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Deep Agents is my first shortlist entry for a general-purpose agent with configurable models and built-in context management.</strong> Claude Agent SDK is a strong fit for embedding Claude Code’s execution behavior. OpenAI Agents SDK and Pydantic AI deserve a trial for application-specific agents, while Pi favors a small extensible core and LangGraph favors explicit workflow control.</p> <p><strong>The best choice depends on the work you intend to accept.</strong> A research assistant, a repository editor, and a service processing customer requests need different tools and recovery rules. These recommendations are editorial judgments from official documentation checked on <strong>October 6, 2026</strong>, not results from a hands-on performance benchmark.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Choose the abstraction first:</strong> assembled agent, application SDK, or workflow runtime.</li> <li><strong>Check execution boundaries:</strong> tool approval, filesystem isolation, and network policy solve different problems.</li> <li><strong>Test recovery:</strong> conversation history alone does not prevent duplicate external actions.</li> <li><strong>Measure accepted work:</strong> include failures, review time, and infrastructure in your cost comparison.</li> <li><strong>Keep the model explicit:</strong> changing both model and agent software tests the complete system, not the software alone.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-a-harness-provides"> <a href="#what-a-harness-provides" title="What a Harness Provides">What a Harness Provides</a> <a href="#what-a-harness-provides" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What a Harness Provides">#</a> </h2> <p>An <strong>agent harness</strong> is the software surrounding a model call. It prepares context, exposes tools, executes approved actions, feeds results back, and decides when to continue or stop. Depending on the implementation, it also manages memory, delegation, permissions, and recovery.</p> <p>A <strong>model</strong> proposes the next action. A <strong>tool</strong> performs an operation. A <strong>runtime</strong> runs and preserves the workflow. These responsibilities overlap in packaged products, but separating them helps you identify missing capabilities.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Component</th> <th>Question to ask</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Context management</strong></td> <td>Which requirements survive a long run?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Tool execution</strong></td> <td>Who validates arguments and limits authority?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>State storage</strong></td> <td>What survives a process restart?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Verification</strong></td> <td>What evidence establishes completion?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Consider an <strong>illustrative support agent</strong> asked to inspect an order and prepare a replacement request. Reading the order, proposing a replacement, and submitting it should have separate authority. A persuasive explanation does not establish permission to submit, and a saved transcript does not establish whether submission already happened.</p> <p><strong>Scope:</strong> this guide compares embeddable software and runtime choices. For daily developer interfaces, use the separate <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI coding-agent comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI coding-agent comparison</a> </span> or <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GUI coding-agent comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >GUI coding-agent comparison</a> </span> . An SDK comparison should not silently become a ranking of terminal tools against editor extensions.</p> <h2 id="the-practical-shortlist"> <a href="#the-practical-shortlist" title="The Practical Shortlist">The Practical Shortlist</a> <a href="#the-practical-shortlist" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The Practical Shortlist">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Starting requirement</th> <th>First option to evaluate</th> <th>Main responsibility you retain</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>General-purpose agent</strong></td> <td>Deep Agents</td> <td>Configure backend, permissions, and model</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Code in an app</strong></td> <td>Claude Agent SDK</td> <td>Operate and isolate the execution process</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Application tool workflow</strong></td> <td>OpenAI Agents SDK</td> <td>Define tools, approvals, and acceptance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Typed Python application</strong></td> <td>Pydantic AI and its Harness package</td> <td>Select capabilities and workspace</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Minimal embeddable coding core</strong></td> <td>Pi SDK</td> <td>Assemble extensions and execution policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Explicit durable workflow</strong></td> <td>LangGraph</td> <td>Design graph state and recovery behavior</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>These are different starting points.</strong> Deep Agents already uses LangGraph, so choosing them is not necessarily an either-or decision. Pydantic AI also separates its core agent framework from assembled harness capabilities. Compare the amount of application code you need to own, rather than treating every row as an interchangeable library.</p> <h2 id="deep-agents-assembled-capabilities"> <a href="#deep-agents-assembled-capabilities" title="Deep Agents: Assembled Capabilities">Deep Agents: Assembled Capabilities</a> <a href="#deep-agents-assembled-capabilities" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Deep Agents: Assembled Capabilities">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose Deep Agents first for an agent working across files, tools, and long conversations.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="official overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview"> <a href="https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >official overview</a> </span> documents filesystem backends, context offloading, summarization, subagents, and human approval. It builds on LangChain and the LangGraph runtime, with integrations for multiple model providers.</p> <p><strong>Configuration still determines behavior.</strong> The current documentation makes task planning opt-in starting with version 0.7. Do not assume a tutorial for an older release describes the current defaults. Record the package version and enabled middleware in your evaluation.</p> <p><strong>Inspect permission scope carefully.</strong> The documented filesystem rules cover built-in file tools, not arbitrary shell commands through sandbox backends. A file-tool denial is insufficient if another execution path reaches the same file. Test the backend and the shell boundary together.</p> <p><strong>My recommendation:</strong> shortlist it for a document-analysis or repository-work service when you want assembled capabilities and provider choice. Prefer a smaller starting point when the job consists of two narrowly defined API calls and a validated response. Extra tools introduce extra behavior to evaluate.</p> <h2 id="claude-embedded-execution"> <a href="#claude-embedded-execution" title="Claude: Embedded Execution">Claude: Embedded Execution</a> <a href="#claude-embedded-execution" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Claude: Embedded Execution">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose Claude Agent SDK when you want Claude Code’s agent inside your application.</strong> Anthropic describes a Python and TypeScript library using the same execution loop, tools, and context management as Claude Code. The SDK runs the Claude Code binary in a process you operate. It is distinct from Anthropic’s basic API client and hosted Managed Agents. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Agent SDK overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Agent SDK overview</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>The attraction is reuse of an existing execution system.</strong> File operations, commands, hooks, permissions, sessions, and subagents arrive as documented capabilities. Your integration supplies the application boundary and task-specific acceptance checks.</p> <p><strong>Hosting remains an engineering decision.</strong> Anthropic’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="deployment guidance"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >deployment guidance</a> </span> discusses filesystem controls, network restrictions, and isolation. Configure those around the process rather than treating a permission prompt as an operating-system boundary.</p> <p><strong>My recommendation:</strong> evaluate it for Claude-centered document or coding automation with substantial file and command work. Choose a provider-flexible alternative if comparing local models and several hosted providers is a core product requirement.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Assembled option</th> <th>Integration emphasis</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Deep Agents</strong></td> <td>Model selection, middleware, and backend configuration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Agent SDK</strong></td> <td>Claude Code execution inside an application process</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="openai-application-tool-workflows"> <a href="#openai-application-tool-workflows" title="OpenAI: Application Tool Workflows">OpenAI: Application Tool Workflows</a> <a href="#openai-application-tool-workflows" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="OpenAI: Application Tool Workflows">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose OpenAI Agents SDK for an application organized around functions, delegated tasks, and explicit outputs.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/"> <a href="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >overview</a> </span> documents the agent loop, handoffs, guardrails, tracing, and sandbox-agent capabilities. The SDK is a builder’s interface, distinct from the Codex developer application.</p> <p><strong>Approval is configurable behavior.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="human-in-the-loop guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/human_in_the_loop/"> <a href="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/human_in_the_loop/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >human-in-the-loop guide</a> </span> describes interrupted runs and serialized state for resuming after a decision. For local shell and patch tools, approval is opt-in. Adding an approval callback alone does not enable the approval requirement.</p> <p><strong>Model support extends beyond OpenAI.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="provider documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/models/"> <a href="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/models/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >provider documentation</a> </span> describes external-provider integration points and adapters. Validate structured outputs, tool calling, and transport support for your selected endpoint instead of assuming feature parity.</p> <p><strong>My recommendation:</strong> shortlist it for a service whose useful actions already exist as well-defined application functions. For example, retrieve an order, calculate eligibility in ordinary code, and prepare a structured request. Keep authorization and eligibility checks in the application even when the model selects the next tool.</p> <h2 id="pydantic-ai-typed-applications"> <a href="#pydantic-ai-typed-applications" title="Pydantic AI: Typed Applications">Pydantic AI: Typed Applications</a> <a href="#pydantic-ai-typed-applications" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Pydantic AI: Typed Applications">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose Pydantic AI when Python types and validated outputs are central to your application.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="core documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/"> <a href="https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >core documentation</a> </span> covers typed tools, dependency injection, structured outputs, and durable-execution integrations. Validation establishes the output’s required structure. It does not establish the truth of every field.</p> <p><strong>The separate Harness package adds assembled capabilities.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/"> <a href="https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >documentation</a> </span> includes Coder and Researcher stacks, filesystem and shell access, memory, and workspace integrations. A local workspace and an isolated sandbox are different execution choices. Relevant harness capabilities require a workspace rather than silently selecting one.</p> <p><strong>My recommendation:</strong> shortlist the core framework for a Python service returning typed records. Add harness capabilities when the task also requires workspace exploration or open-ended research. This keeps a bounded extraction service from inheriting shell access without a concrete need.</p> <p>For an <strong>illustrative invoice-review agent</strong>, schema validation checks whether a total is numeric and a currency belongs to an allowed set. Separate application logic compares the total against line items and verifies source evidence. Both checks belong in the trial.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Application concern</th> <th>Acceptance check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Structured output</strong></td> <td>Validate fields and independently verify their meaning</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Approval pause</strong></td> <td>Persist the exact pending action and decision</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Provider change</strong></td> <td>Repeat tool-call and output compatibility tests</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="pi-small-extensible-core"> <a href="#pi-small-extensible-core" title="Pi: Small Extensible Core">Pi: Small Extensible Core</a> <a href="#pi-small-extensible-core" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Pi: Small Extensible Core">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose Pi’s SDK when you want direct control over a compact coding-agent implementation.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="project documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/coding-agent"> <a href="https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/coding-agent" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >project documentation</a> </span> describes SDK and RPC integration alongside its interactive interface. Its default tool set consists of reading, writing, editing, and shell execution, with extensions for additional behavior.</p> <p><strong>Minimalism shifts work to the integrator.</strong> Pi deliberately omits built-in permission popups and subagent orchestration. Its documentation directs users toward containers or custom extensions for confirmation flows. Evaluate the embedded SDK here, not its terminal interface against another vendor’s graphical editor.</p> <p><strong>My recommendation:</strong> shortlist Pi for a bespoke coding service when you are prepared to own execution restrictions, extension review, and recovery policy. Its small core is attractive for understanding and changing behavior. It is a less suitable starting point when your main requirement is an already assembled approval and orchestration system.</p> <h2 id="langgraph-explicit-workflow-control"> <a href="#langgraph-explicit-workflow-control" title="LangGraph: Explicit Workflow Control">LangGraph: Explicit Workflow Control</a> <a href="#langgraph-explicit-workflow-control" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="LangGraph: Explicit Workflow Control">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose LangGraph when the workflow itself needs explicit state and transitions.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="persistence documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence"> <a href="https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >persistence documentation</a> </span> distinguishes thread-scoped checkpoints from cross-thread stores. A persistent checkpointer supports recovery across process restarts. An in-memory checkpointer does not.</p> <p><strong>LangGraph is a runtime foundation.</strong> You define the workflow and decide where model-driven behavior belongs. Deep Agents already uses this foundation, so dropping to LangGraph makes sense when you need more direct control over execution paths.</p> <p><strong>My recommendation:</strong> shortlist it for a process with named stages, review pauses, and distinct recovery rules. A document-intake workflow might extract fields, validate them, request review, and publish an approved record. Fixed transitions are useful when a model should choose content but should not invent the business process.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Workflow stage</th> <th>Completion evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Extract</strong></td> <td>Source-linked candidate record</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Validate</strong></td> <td>Deterministic checks and exceptions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Review</strong></td> <td>Decision attached to the specific candidate</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Publish</strong></td> <td>External receipt recorded against the operation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>External effects need their own recovery design.</strong> Saving graph state does not make a remote service transaction atomic with the checkpoint. Use an operation identifier and reconcile the external result before retrying a submission.</p> <h2 id="test-the-missing-pieces"> <a href="#test-the-missing-pieces" title="Test the Missing Pieces">Test the Missing Pieces</a> <a href="#test-the-missing-pieces" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Test the Missing Pieces">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A feature list is only a starting point.</strong> Run each candidate through failures which resemble your workload. Use a disposable workspace and test services with synthetic records.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Test</th> <th>Evidence to retain</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Interrupted submission</strong></td> <td>One external effect after recovery</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Long conversation</strong></td> <td>Original requirements still satisfied</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Rejected action</strong></td> <td>No effect through an alternate tool</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Untrusted document instruction</strong></td> <td>Document text does not acquire authority</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Malformed tool arguments</strong></td> <td>Rejection before application mutation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Budget exhaustion</strong></td> <td>Bounded stop with inspectable partial work</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Define repetition explicitly.</strong> For a replacement-request service, stop the worker after the test service accepts a request but before local completion is saved. On restart, the workflow should look up the operation identifier instead of blindly submitting again. This is a proposed test, not an observed result for the listed products.</p> <p><strong>Check evidence after compaction.</strong> Put an important requirement early in the task, then supply enough realistic material to trigger the configured context strategy. Ask the agent to produce its final artifact and supporting source references. Our <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLM and agent-memory analysis"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/context-language-models-agent-memory-hallucinations/"> <a href="/articles/context-language-models-agent-memory-hallucinations/" rel="follow me" >CLM and agent-memory analysis</a> </span> explains why retaining notes and retaining accurate evidence are separate concerns.</p> <p><strong>Review telemetry destinations.</strong> Tool traces and memory stores often contain task data. Record which systems receive them and how long they remain available. Local model inference does not imply local-only logging, retrieval, or execution.</p> <h2 id="compare-cost-per-accepted-task"> <a href="#compare-cost-per-accepted-task" title="Compare Cost Per Accepted Task">Compare Cost Per Accepted Task</a> <a href="#compare-cost-per-accepted-task" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare Cost Per Accepted Task">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use two evaluation tracks.</strong> A controlled comparison holds the model, tools, task set, and budgets steady where supported. A deployment comparison uses each candidate’s intended configuration. The first isolates some software effects. The second answers which complete setup serves your work better.</p> <p><strong>Do not force unsupported configurations into the controlled track.</strong> If two candidates lack a common model or tool interface, report the comparison as a system evaluation. Keep setup effort and human steering in the record.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Illustrative trial record, not a framework configuration file</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">candidate</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"package and pinned version"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">model</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"provider and exact model identifier"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">workspace</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"isolated test environment"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">task_set</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"frozen fixtures and acceptance checks"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">limits</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">elapsed_minutes</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">15</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">model_calls</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">30</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">tool_calls</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">60</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">record</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">accepted_result</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">unsupported_claims</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">duplicate_external_actions</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">inference_cost</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">infrastructure_cost</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">human_review_minutes</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">recovery_outcome</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Run several trials per task.</strong> Keep unsuccessful attempts in the denominator and report raw counts alongside percentages. A small trial reveals failure patterns, not a stable industry ranking.</p> <p><strong>Illustrative cost calculation:</strong> suppose setup A spends $12 across ten attempts and produces eight accepted results. Its inference cost per accepted task is $1.50. Setup B spends $8 but produces four accepted results, so its corresponding cost is $2.00. Neither number includes human review or infrastructure, which belong in a separate recorded total.</p> <p><strong>Set disqualifying failures before testing.</strong> An unauthorized submission or cross-user data leak should not disappear inside an average quality score. After enforcing those requirements, compare correctness, recovery, review effort, and cost.</p> <h2 id="make-a-bounded-choice"> <a href="#make-a-bounded-choice" title="Make a Bounded Choice">Make a Bounded Choice</a> <a href="#make-a-bounded-choice" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Make a Bounded Choice">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start with two candidates and one real workflow.</strong> For an assembled provider-flexible agent, compare Deep Agents with a narrower alternative suited to your application. For Claude Code behavior inside a service, trial Claude Agent SDK. For typed application work, compare Pydantic AI with OpenAI Agents SDK. Choose Pi when custom behavior is worth additional integration work, and LangGraph when explicit workflow control is the priority.</p> <p><strong>Prerequisites for the trial:</strong> approved model access, synthetic fixtures, an isolated workspace where needed, and written acceptance criteria. Allow an initial afternoon for setup and basic failure tests, then collect repeated runs before making a production decision. Difficulty is intermediate to advanced, depending on external actions and recovery requirements.</p> <p><strong>Select the smallest system which passes your requirements.</strong> Preserve the trial fixtures, package versions, and failure records. Rerun them when changing the model, context strategy, tools, or execution backend. Those changes alter the system you evaluated.</p> <h2 id="references"> <a href="#references" title="References">References</a> <a href="#references" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="References">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="LangChain: Deep Agents overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview"> <a href="https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >LangChain: Deep Agents overview</a> </span> </li> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Anthropic: Claude Agent SDK overview"> <meta itemprop="url" overview</a> </span> </li> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Anthropic: Secure deployment"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Anthropic: Secure deployment</a> </span> </li> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenAI: Agents SDK"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/"> <a href="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >OpenAI: Agents SDK</a> </span> </li> <li> item.title: Claude Code CLI vs Desktop: 2026 Workflow Comparison
item.description: Compare Claude Code in the terminal and desktop Code workspace, including shared settings, session handoff, scripting, visual review, and permission choices.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Claude Code CLI and desktop</strong> provide two ways to direct Anthropic’s coding agent. The CLI favors shell workflows and programmatic invocation. Desktop favors a visible project workspace with file changes and review alongside the conversation.</p> <p><strong>This comparison concerns the desktop coding workspace</strong>, described as the Code tab in Anthropic’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="desktop quick start"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >desktop quick start</a> </span> . General chat and other desktop workflows are outside its scope. The distinction matters when checking repository access and configuration.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Use the CLI for scripts</strong>, piped input, and terminal-centered work.</li> <li><strong>Use desktop for graphical supervision</strong>, attachments, and diff review.</li> <li><strong>Shared configuration reduces duplication</strong>, but session behavior and available controls differ.</li> <li><strong>Moving a conversation requires supported handoff</strong>, not copying a prompt into a new chat.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Scope and date:</strong> Official documentation checked on October 6, 2026. This is a feature and workflow comparison, not a coding benchmark. You need a testable repository and an approved account route. Allow 45–60 minutes for a small trial.</p> <h2 id="same-engine-different-controls"> <a href="#same-engine-different-controls" title="Same Engine, Different Controls">Same Engine, Different Controls</a> <a href="#same-engine-different-controls" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Same Engine, Different Controls">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Anthropic describes desktop as the same underlying engine with a GUI.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="desktop reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >desktop reference</a> </span> documents shared configuration and project memory, while distinguishing client features. Shared foundations do not imply every CLI flag has a desktop button.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Activity</th> <th>CLI</th> <th>Desktop Code workspace</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Interactive work</strong></td> <td>Terminal conversation</td> <td>Graphical conversation with project panes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Scripted invocation</strong></td> <td>Print mode and piped input</td> <td>Use the CLI for this workflow</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Change review</strong></td> <td>Terminal/editor workflow</td> <td>Integrated visual diff</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Task organization</strong></td> <td>Terminal sessions and CLI controls</td> <td>Session sidebar and workspace layout</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recurring work</strong></td> <td>External scheduler or CI</td> <td>Desktop scheduled tasks</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Project rules</strong></td> <td>Repository and user configuration</td> <td>Shared settings with surface-specific behavior</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Choose based on supervision effort.</strong> A shell-heavy bug investigation and a visual application change place different demands on the interface. Neither is evidence of a stronger model.</p> <h2 id="terminal-work-and-scripts"> <a href="#terminal-work-and-scripts" title="Terminal Work and Scripts">Terminal Work and Scripts</a> <a href="#terminal-work-and-scripts" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Terminal Work and Scripts">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>claude -p <span style="color:#e6db74">"Explain the failing test and propose a fix. Do not edit files."</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Print mode runs without the normal interactive conversation.</strong> Anthropic’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI reference</a> </span> documents this command family, piped input, and resume options. Match tool permissions to the investigation. The prompt above does not substitute for a read-only policy.</p> <p><strong>Use a script when the input and output contract is stable.</strong> Examples include a scheduled report, a bounded repository inspection, or a CI step producing review material. Define what counts as failure and save the evidence. Avoid approving a patch solely because the agent’s final message sounds complete.</p> <p><strong>Keep interactive work interactive when decisions remain open.</strong> If a task requires choosing an API design or resolving contradictory requirements, a terminal session with explicit checkpoints often needs less automation code than a headless wrapper.</p> <h2 id="desktop-review-and-scheduling"> <a href="#desktop-review-and-scheduling" title="Desktop Review and Scheduling">Desktop Review and Scheduling</a> <a href="#desktop-review-and-scheduling" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Desktop Review and Scheduling">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Desktop supplies a coding workspace without requiring a separate CLI installation.</strong> The quick start describes project selection, model selection, and graphical acceptance of changes. Evaluate it with a patch spanning a source file, a test, and a configuration file so review involves more than one pane.</p> <p><strong>Scheduled work is a separate desktop feature.</strong> Anthropic’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="scheduled-task documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >scheduled-task documentation</a> </span> explains recurring tasks and their operating requirements. Check where a scheduled task runs and what must remain available before relying on it for a daily workflow.</p> <p><strong>Review the aggregate patch.</strong> Individual edit approvals do not reveal every interaction between changed files. After the run, inspect the final diff and execute the acceptance check independently.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/claude-cli-desktop-session-handoff.webp", "caption": "Terminal conversation and graphical code review connected through a shared project with a controlled session handoff", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.4292252 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.394839890", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.4292252 +0000 UTC m=+546.394839890"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/claude-cli-desktop-session-handoff.webp" alt="Terminal conversation and graphical code review connected through a shared project with a controlled session handoff"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>A shared engine still needs explicit session and environment checks</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="settings-and-permissions"> <a href="#settings-and-permissions" title="Settings and Permissions">Settings and Permissions</a> <a href="#settings-and-permissions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Settings and Permissions">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Settings have scope and precedence.</strong> Anthropic’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="settings reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >settings reference</a> </span> distinguishes managed, user, project, and local configuration. Verify the effective setup before diagnosing a client difference. A project rule does not necessarily override organization policy.</p> <p><strong>Permission mode changes the interaction.</strong> Compare both clients under matching policies, then test your preferred policy separately. Do not present fewer approval prompts as an unconditional advantage. The relevant question is whether the permitted actions match the task and your environment.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Configuration check</th> <th>Reason</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Project folder</strong></td> <td>Loads the intended code and project rules</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Account route</strong></td> <td>Determines access and billing context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Selected model</strong></td> <td>Avoids mixing interface and model changes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Permission policy</strong></td> <td>Controls which operations proceed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Runtime environment</strong></td> <td>Determines available commands and tests</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Keep canonical project instructions in the repository.</strong> Document build commands, excluded files, and acceptance criteria. Ask the agent to identify those constraints before editing. A mismatch signals a configuration issue to resolve before benchmarking behavior.</p> <h2 id="moving-a-session"> <a href="#moving-a-session" title="Moving a Session">Moving a Session</a> <a href="#moving-a-session" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Moving a Session">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>/desktop </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The documented CLI-to-desktop handoff saves the session and exits the CLI.</strong> The desktop reference limits this command to supported macOS and x64 Windows subscription sessions. API-key and third-party-provider sessions do not receive the same handoff path. Check the installed version and account before depending on it.</p> <p><strong>Treat handoff as a controlled transition.</strong> Finish or stop the active operation, identify the current branch, and inspect pending changes. After opening the destination interface, verify the repository and ask for the next planned step. Do not launch a second implementation against the same files while the first still runs.</p> <p><strong>Sharing files differs from sharing a conversation.</strong> Two clients opening the same checkout see filesystem changes, but a fresh conversation lacks the reasoning and constraints of the original session. Preserve a short task record in the repository when you need a portable handover.</p> <h2 id="choose-through-a-small-trial"> <a href="#choose-through-a-small-trial" title="Choose Through a Small Trial">Choose Through a Small Trial</a> <a href="#choose-through-a-small-trial" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose Through a Small Trial">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use a bug with a visible symptom.</strong> Supply the reproduction, expected behavior, and the files the agent must preserve. Run separate attempts from the same base revision, with matching model and permission settings.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Trial stage</th> <th>Observe</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Context</strong></td> <td>Effort attaching logs, files, and screenshots</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Implementation</strong></td> <td>Interruptions and clarification needs</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Review</strong></td> <td>Ease of inspecting every changed file</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Correction</strong></td> <td>Response to a rejected approach</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Completion</strong></td> <td>Independent test result and clean diff</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Prefer the CLI</strong> when scripts and terminal context dominate. <strong>Prefer desktop</strong> when visible project state and graphical review reduce friction. Use both deliberately if you alternate between those needs.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-next-steps"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">Troubleshooting and Next Steps</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>If desktop lacks a command found in the CLI</strong>, consult the feature comparison instead of assuming an installation failure. If commands work only in the terminal, compare execution environment and runtime discovery. If handoff is unavailable, verify platform and authentication eligibility.</p> <p><strong>For a broader shortlist</strong>, read the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI comparison</a> </span> or <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GUI comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >GUI comparison</a> </span> . For a cross-vendor agent comparison, see <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode vs Claude Code"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/opencode-vs-claude-code/"> <a href="/articles/opencode-vs-claude-code/" rel="follow me" >OpenCode vs Claude Code</a> </span> .</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: CLI Coding Agents Compared: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Copilot, and Aider
item.description: Compare six terminal coding agents by workflow, automation, model access, permissions, and review effort. Build a shortlist with a repeatable repository trial.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Terminal coding agents</strong> share a familiar interface but differ in how they gather context, edit files, request approval, and fit into scripts. This guide compares Claude Code CLI, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Aider. It evaluates their terminal workflows, independently of each vendor’s desktop products.</p> <p><strong>Start with your constraints.</strong> Provider access, repeatable automation, and review habits are better filters than a generic leaderboard. The recommendations below are editorial judgments based on official documentation checked on October 6, 2026, not measured performance rankings.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI</strong> deserve a trial when you want their respective first-party model workflows.</li> <li><strong>OpenCode and Aider</strong> suit experiments across model providers, with different approaches to interaction and editing.</li> <li><strong>Copilot CLI</strong> deserves consideration when GitHub access and organization policy already shape your workflow.</li> <li><strong>A terminal interface does not imply local inference</strong>, unrestricted model choice, or unattended execution.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> Git, a disposable checkout, working tests, and approved model credentials. Difficulty is intermediate. Allow one afternoon to compare two shortlisted tools across three small tasks.</p> <h2 id="the-shortlist"> <a href="#the-shortlist" title="The Shortlist">The Shortlist</a> <a href="#the-shortlist" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The Shortlist">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Terminal tool</th> <th>Reason to evaluate</th> <th>Decision to resolve</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Code CLI</strong></td> <td>Claude-centered repository work</td> <td>Account route and permission policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Codex CLI</strong></td> <td>Interactive work plus scripted execution</td> <td>Sandbox settings and output handling</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Gemini CLI</strong></td> <td>Gemini workflow and structured headless output</td> <td>Authentication, quotas, and tool policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>OpenCode CLI</strong></td> <td>Provider selection and configurable agents</td> <td>Model and endpoint compatibility</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Copilot CLI</strong></td> <td>Copilot access from your shell</td> <td>Organization access and tool approval</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Aider</strong></td> <td>Git-focused pair programming</td> <td>File selection and editing model</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>This is a bounded shortlist.</strong> It compares six established terminal workflows, not every product offering a CLI. Graphical editors and extensions belong in the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GUI coding-agent comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >GUI coding-agent comparison</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="claude-code-and-codex"> <a href="#claude-code-and-codex" title="Claude Code and Codex">Claude Code and Codex</a> <a href="#claude-code-and-codex" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Claude Code and Codex">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Claude Code CLI</strong> offers interactive sessions, resumable conversations, piped input, and a print mode for scripts. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI reference</a> </span> documents those entry points. Trial it if you want Claude working through repository changes while you direct tasks from the shell.</p> <p><strong>Codex CLI</strong> exposes repository inspection, edits, command execution, and review in a terminal interface. OpenAI’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI documentation</a> </span> describes the interactive controls. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="non-interactive mode"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >non-interactive mode</a> </span> provides <code>codex exec</code> for scripts and continuous integration.</p> <p><strong>Choose between these through completed work.</strong> Give each an unfamiliar bug and an existing failing test. Compare its explanation, patch scope, test selection, and recovery after a rejected approach. A confident final message is not evidence of correctness.</p> <h2 id="gemini-cli-and-copilot"> <a href="#gemini-cli-and-copilot" title="Gemini CLI and Copilot">Gemini CLI and Copilot</a> <a href="#gemini-cli-and-copilot" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Gemini CLI and Copilot">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Gemini CLI</strong> documents project context, extensions, tool execution, and automation in its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="official guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://geminicli.com/docs/"> <a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >official guide</a> </span> . Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="headless reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/headless/"> <a href="https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/headless/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >headless reference</a> </span> specifies structured output and exit codes. This makes output handling a concrete part of a trial, rather than an assumption based on terminal availability.</p> <p><strong>GitHub Copilot CLI</strong> supports interactive work and programmatic prompts through the current standalone <code>copilot</code> command. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="product documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-cli"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-cli" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >product documentation</a> </span> covers planning and tool permissions. Evaluate it against the account and policies your team uses, rather than treating GitHub branding as automatic access to every repository or service.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Automation entry</th> <th>Documented command family</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Code</strong></td> <td><code>claude -p</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Codex</strong></td> <td><code>codex exec</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Gemini CLI</strong></td> <td><code>gemini -p</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Copilot CLI</strong></td> <td><code>copilot -p</code></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Headless mode needs an execution policy.</strong> Define allowed actions, time limits, error handling, and artifact collection before putting an agent in a pipeline. A process exiting successfully does not prove the resulting code meets your acceptance criteria.</p> <h2 id="opencode-and-aider"> <a href="#opencode-and-aider" title="OpenCode and Aider">OpenCode and Aider</a> <a href="#opencode-and-aider" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="OpenCode and Aider">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>OpenCode CLI</strong> combines an interactive terminal UI with command-line operations. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI reference</a> </span> documents <code>opencode run</code>, while its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="provider guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >provider guide</a> </span> describes model connections. Trial it when provider flexibility matters enough to justify managing compatibility and billing details.</p> <p><strong>Aider</strong> centers on pair programming in a Git repository. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://aider.chat/docs/"> <a href="https://aider.chat/docs/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >documentation</a> </span> covers file selection, repository maps, model connections, and lint/test integration. Trial it when you prefer to direct a bounded editing conversation and keep repository changes close to an explicit Git workflow.</p> <p><strong>Different interaction styles deserve different expectations.</strong> A narrowly scoped editing assistant and an agent exploring a whole repository do not consume context in identical ways. Record the files supplied, the exploration allowed, and the human steering required. Do not award a tool a productivity win after quietly doing its context selection yourself.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/terminal-agent-evaluation-flow.webp", "caption": "Abstract terminal sessions feeding a shared patch review, test checklist, and task cost record", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.436123672 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.401738362", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.436123672 +0000 UTC m=+546.401738362"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/terminal-agent-evaluation-flow.webp" alt="Abstract terminal sessions feeding a shared patch review, test checklist, and task cost record"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Use the same acceptance criteria across every terminal workflow</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="models-access-and-cost"> <a href="#models-access-and-cost" title="Models, Access, and Cost">Models, Access, and Cost</a> <a href="#models-access-and-cost" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Models, Access, and Cost">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>The agent is the software around the model.</strong> It builds requests, handles tool results, manages conversation state, and applies execution policy. The model and serving endpoint influence reasoning, tool-call reliability, latency, and available context.</p> <p><strong>Provider flexibility has operational costs.</strong> A custom endpoint adds decisions about model identifiers, context settings, authentication, and tool support. An integrated service reduces some setup choices while tying access to its account and policies. Neither arrangement establishes a universal quality ranking.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Cost category</th> <th>Include in the trial</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Account allowance</strong></td> <td>Included access, rate limits, and exhaustion behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Metered inference</strong></td> <td>Prompt, output, cache, and retry usage</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Local serving</strong></td> <td>Hardware, electricity, and runtime maintenance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Human effort</strong></td> <td>Setup, corrections, and final review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Failed work</strong></td> <td>Abandoned runs and reverted patches</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Compare cost per accepted change.</strong> Keep subscription fees separate from incremental API charges and developer time. A free client with paid inference differs from a subscription with an allowance. Recheck current account terms before changing providers.</p> <h2 id="permissions-and-repository-context"> <a href="#permissions-and-repository-context" title="Permissions and Repository Context">Permissions and Repository Context</a> <a href="#permissions-and-repository-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Permissions and Repository Context">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Approval and isolation are different controls.</strong> An approval prompt asks whether an action should proceed. A sandbox limits the resources available to an executed action. Check both, including file access, network access, and commands spawned by tools.</p> <p><strong>Codex’s permission documentation</strong> explicitly separates filesystem and network rules, including conditions for enforcing destination restrictions. Use its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="permission reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >permission reference</a> </span> to inspect the installed setup. For any shortlisted tool, test a harmless allowed action and a harmless prohibited action before relying on policy.</p> <p><strong>Project instructions need verification.</strong> Give each tool the same build command, acceptance criteria, and exclusions through its supported instruction mechanism. Ask it to repeat the active constraints before editing. A missing instruction file is a setup defect, not a model benchmark.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Task: Fix the supplied reproduction without changing the public API. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Scope: Preserve unrelated work and avoid new dependencies. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Evidence: Run the existing regression test and relevant neighboring tests. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Report: Explain the cause, changed files, checks, and remaining uncertainty. </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>This trial prompt is intentionally bounded.</strong> Add a known reproduction and independently written checks. Use the same starting commit in separate checkouts. Record tool version, model, provider, permission policy, elapsed time, and interventions.</p> <h2 id="pick-your-first-pair"> <a href="#pick-your-first-pair" title="Pick Your First Pair">Pick Your First Pair</a> <a href="#pick-your-first-pair" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Pick Your First Pair">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Your priority</th> <th>Start the trial with</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Claude versus OpenAI workflow</strong></td> <td>Claude Code CLI and Codex CLI</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Google versus OpenAI workflow</strong></td> <td>Gemini CLI and Codex CLI</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Provider flexibility</strong></td> <td>OpenCode CLI and Aider</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Existing GitHub deployment</strong></td> <td>Copilot CLI and one approved alternative</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Claude versus configurable providers</strong></td> <td>Claude Code CLI and OpenCode CLI</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Run three tasks per tool:</strong> a reproduced bug, a small feature with independent tests, and a constrained refactor. Keep failed attempts. Review patches without looking at which agent produced them if practical. The winner is the workflow producing acceptable changes with less total effort in your repository.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-next-steps"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">Troubleshooting and Next Steps</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Unexpected results often start in configuration.</strong> Missing tools, wrong working directories, different model versions, or exhausted allowances distort comparisons. Verify those before rewriting prompts repeatedly.</p> <p><strong>Continue with a focused guide:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode vs Claude Code"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/opencode-vs-claude-code/"> <a href="/articles/opencode-vs-claude-code/" rel="follow me" >OpenCode vs Claude Code</a> </span> , <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Codex CLI vs desktop"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/codex-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/codex-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >Codex CLI vs desktop</a> </span> , <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Claude Code CLI vs desktop"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/claude-code-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/claude-code-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >Claude Code CLI vs desktop</a> </span> , <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode CLI vs desktop"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/opencode-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/opencode-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >OpenCode CLI vs desktop</a> </span> , or <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Copilot CLI vs VS Code"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/github-copilot-cli-vs-vscode/"> <a href="/articles/github-copilot-cli-vs-vscode/" rel="follow me" >Copilot CLI vs VS Code</a> </span> . Those interface comparisons stay within each product family.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Codex CLI vs Desktop: 2026 Workflow Comparison
item.description: Choose between Codex in the terminal and OpenAI’s desktop coding workspace. Compare scripting, worktrees, visual review, schedules, and execution environments.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Codex CLI</strong> fits a shell-driven workflow with explicit commands and scriptable runs. <strong>Codex on desktop</strong> fits work organized around projects, conversations, visual outputs, and review panels. Choose the interface around how you supervise work, while keeping the model, repository, and execution policy consistent.</p> <p><strong>Naming note:</strong> OpenAI’s former Codex app documentation now redirects to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="ChatGPT desktop app documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >ChatGPT desktop app documentation</a> </span> . This guide uses “Codex desktop” for the coding workflow in the application. It does not equate an ordinary chat without repository access with a coding agent.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Use the CLI for shell composition</strong> and repeatable programmatic runs.</li> <li><strong>Use desktop for project organization</strong>, visual review, and scheduled-task management.</li> <li><strong>Keep execution location explicit</strong>, especially when working through remote connections.</li> <li><strong>The interface does not guarantee better code</strong> or create an independent inference allowance.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Scope and date:</strong> Official documentation checked on October 6, 2026. Recommendations concern workflow, not measured model performance. Prerequisites are a repository, working tests, and suitable account access. Allow an hour for a small cross-interface trial.</p> <h2 id="compare-the-workflows"> <a href="#compare-the-workflows" title="Compare the Workflows">Compare the Workflows</a> <a href="#compare-the-workflows" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare the Workflows">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Need</th> <th>Codex CLI</th> <th>Codex desktop</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Start repository work</strong></td> <td>Launch from a shell directory</td> <td>Select a project and execution environment</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Repeat a scripted task</strong></td> <td><code>codex exec</code></td> <td>Prepare prompts and inspect outputs visually</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Inspect several tasks</strong></td> <td>Terminal/session workflow</td> <td>Project and chat organization</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Review changes</strong></td> <td>Terminal commands and review controls</td> <td>Diff and review panels</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Manage schedules</strong></td> <td>External job runner around a script</td> <td>Scheduled-task management interface</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Isolate changes</strong></td> <td>Choose a separate checkout/worktree</td> <td>Integrated worktree workflow</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Shared agent foundations matter.</strong> OpenAI describes the CLI, app, and IDE extension as interfaces around its agent runtime in <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Codex as a platform"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://developers.openai.com/blog/codex-as-a-platform"> <a href="https://developers.openai.com/blog/codex-as-a-platform" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Codex as a platform</a> </span> . The runtime manages state, tools, and policy. Interface differences still affect what context you supply and how you inspect the result.</p> <h2 id="where-the-cli-fits"> <a href="#where-the-cli-fits" title="Where the CLI Fits">Where the CLI Fits</a> <a href="#where-the-cli-fits" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Where the CLI Fits">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>codex </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Launch from the intended repository.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI guide</a> </span> documents interactive inspection, editing, commands, and review. Use this route when your existing workflow already revolves around terminal sessions and command output.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>codex exec <span style="color:#e6db74">"Identify the documented test command. Do not modify files."</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Use <code>codex exec</code> for a bounded scripted task.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="non-interactive reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >non-interactive reference</a> </span> explains how progress and final output are emitted. Apply an appropriate read-only execution policy when investigating. A sentence asking for no edits is an instruction, not an enforced filesystem boundary.</p> <p><strong>A production script needs more than this example.</strong> Define credentials, repository selection, timeout, permissions, output storage, and failure handling. Have the job produce evidence for a reviewer before considering automated changes. Keep the execution contract in version control so a later operator knows what the agent was allowed to do.</p> <h2 id="where-desktop-fits"> <a href="#where-desktop-fits" title="Where Desktop Fits">Where Desktop Fits</a> <a href="#where-desktop-fits" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Where Desktop Fits">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Desktop organizes related work in one workspace.</strong> OpenAI’s current app documentation describes project switching, file inspection, connected tools, and long-running tasks. This supports a workflow in which you move between implementation, a rendered artifact, and review without reconstructing context from multiple terminal windows.</p> <p><strong>Review is a concrete differentiator.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="code-review documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/code-review"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/code-review" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >code-review documentation</a> </span> describes viewing descriptions, changed files, comments, and checks. Use these views to investigate a patch, then decide whether it meets the requirement. A reviewer still needs independent evidence for behavior outside the diff.</p> <p><strong>Try desktop on a visual task.</strong> Ask for a small layout fix with a screenshot and explicit viewport requirements. Compare the effort needed to attach context, inspect the result, and request one correction. Measure human review time separately from the model’s response time.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/codex-terminal-desktop-review.webp", "caption": "Terminal automation and desktop review panels connected to the same repository and independent validation checklist", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.441181586 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.406796275", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.441181586 +0000 UTC m=+546.406796275"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/codex-terminal-desktop-review.webp" alt="Terminal automation and desktop review panels connected to the same repository and independent validation checklist"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Keep the repository and acceptance criteria constant while comparing interfaces</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="worktrees-and-execution-location"> <a href="#worktrees-and-execution-location" title="Worktrees and Execution Location">Worktrees and Execution Location</a> <a href="#worktrees-and-execution-location" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Worktrees and Execution Location">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A worktree is another checkout of a Git repository.</strong> OpenAI’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="worktree guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/git-worktrees"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/git-worktrees" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >worktree guide</a> </span> describes isolated parallel chats and moving work between the local checkout and a managed worktree. The files and commands stay on the computer or development environment hosting the project.</p> <p><strong>Isolation does not merge the result.</strong> Review the diff, run checks, and decide how to bring changes into your intended branch. Dependencies, ignored files, and external services also need attention when starting from a fresh checkout.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Before a task</th> <th>Confirm</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Repository</strong></td> <td>Correct project and base revision</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Checkout</strong></td> <td>Existing directory or isolated worktree</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution host</strong></td> <td>Computer containing files and tools</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Environment</strong></td> <td>Runtime, dependencies, and test services</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Permissions</strong></td> <td>Allowed file writes and network access</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Use the same environment in your comparison.</strong> A desktop task on a configured workstation and a CLI task in a minimal container test more than interface preference. Record environmental differences before attributing failures to the client.</p> <h2 id="scheduling-and-permissions"> <a href="#scheduling-and-permissions" title="Scheduling and Permissions">Scheduling and Permissions</a> <a href="#scheduling-and-permissions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Scheduling and Permissions">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Desktop provides schedule management.</strong> OpenAI’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="scheduled-task guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/automations"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/automations" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >scheduled-task guide</a> </span> distinguishes the management interface from the CLI. Local scheduled work requires the relevant computer and application to remain available. A shell scheduler around <code>codex exec</code> is a separate operational arrangement.</p> <p><strong>Permissions apply to the execution environment.</strong> Check the effective profile rather than inferring safety from a terminal or graphical prompt. OpenAI’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="permissions reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions"> <a href="https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >permissions reference</a> </span> documents filesystem and network boundaries. A GUI approval and a sandbox policy solve different problems.</p> <p><strong>Account access needs its own check.</strong> Confirm the active sign-in, available model, and usage display in each interface. Do not budget as though opening a second client creates another independent allowance. Record the billing route before comparing per-task costs.</p> <h2 id="a-one-hour-trial"> <a href="#a-one-hour-trial" title="A One-Hour Trial">A One-Hour Trial</a> <a href="#a-one-hour-trial" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="A One-Hour Trial">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Prepare one bounded change</strong> with an independent acceptance test and a clean baseline.</li> <li><strong>Run it in each interface</strong> from separate checkouts with matching model and policy settings.</li> <li><strong>Request one correction</strong> after inspecting the first patch.</li> <li><strong>Review the final diff</strong> and run the same verification commands.</li> <li><strong>Record your effort</strong> supplying context, finding output, and approving the result.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Choose the CLI</strong> if the task becomes easier to repeat and inspect through shell tools. <strong>Choose desktop</strong> if project organization and visual review reduce your supervision effort. Keeping both installed is reasonable when each serves a distinct part of your workflow.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-next-steps"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">Troubleshooting and Next Steps</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A missing file usually warrants an environment check.</strong> Verify project, checkout, and execution host before asking the agent to recreate anything. For differing test results, compare runtime selection and dependency setup.
