For a stalled local schedule, confirm the application and computer were available.</p> <p><strong>Compare vendors separately.</strong> Use the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI master comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI master comparison</a> </span> for terminal alternatives and the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GUI master comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >GUI master comparison</a> </span> for graphical editors and extensions. Keep the model and task record from this trial for future upgrades.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: GitHub Copilot CLI vs VS Code: 2026 Workflow Comparison
item.description: Compare Copilot’s terminal agent with its VS Code experience, including editor context, visual diffs, agent mode, CLI integration, and account policies.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>GitHub Copilot CLI and Copilot in VS Code serve different entry points into coding work.</strong> The CLI starts with your shell and a task prompt. VS Code combines editor context, suggestions, chat, and agent workflows. Both deserve evaluation within the same account and repository policy.</p> <p><strong>The choice is not exclusive.</strong> GitHub documents a connection between Copilot CLI and VS Code. A terminal-driven task still benefits from editor selections and visual review when you explicitly connect the two.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Use Copilot CLI for terminal-driven tasks</strong> and supported programmatic invocation.</li> <li><strong>Use Copilot in VS Code for editor-centered work</strong>, including inline assistance and Agent mode.</li> <li><strong>Connect the CLI to VS Code</strong> when you want terminal prompts with editor context and diffs.</li> <li><strong>Account, model, and policy settings require verification</strong>, even within one product family.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Scope and date:</strong> Official documentation checked on October 6, 2026. This compares the standalone <code>copilot</code> CLI with Copilot in VS Code, not the old <code>gh copilot</code> extension or a cloud agent assigned a GitHub issue. Prerequisites are a testable repository and permitted Copilot access. Allow an hour for a trial.</p> <h2 id="three-ways-to-work"> <a href="#three-ways-to-work" title="Three Ways to Work">Three Ways to Work</a> <a href="#three-ways-to-work" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Three Ways to Work">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Workflow</th> <th>Main interaction</th> <th>Good trial task</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Standalone CLI</strong></td> <td>Terminal prompt and command output</td> <td>Explain and fix a reproduced test failure</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>VS Code integration</strong></td> <td>Editor selection, chat, suggestions, and diffs</td> <td>Modify a selected function and its tests</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>CLI connected to VS Code</strong></td> <td>Terminal task with editor context and review</td> <td>Investigate from the shell, inspect the patch visually</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>The hybrid remains a CLI session.</strong> Running it inside an integrated terminal does not automatically turn it into the editor’s native Agent-mode conversation. Check the active session and connection instead of relying on the window containing the prompt.</p> <h2 id="what-the-cli-provides"> <a href="#what-the-cli-provides" title="What the CLI Provides">What the CLI Provides</a> <a href="#what-the-cli-provides" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What the CLI Provides">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>copilot </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The current standalone command starts the terminal agent.</strong> GitHub’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Copilot CLI overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-cli"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-cli" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Copilot CLI overview</a> </span> describes interactive and programmatic use. It also documents planning and tool permissions. Evaluate it where terminal output is already the main evidence for a task.</p> <p><strong>A strong first task has a concrete failure.</strong> Supply the failing command, expected behavior, and a restriction against unrelated refactoring. Ask the agent to reproduce the issue before changing files. Review whether its final explanation matches the observed test output.</p> <p><strong>Automation requires explicit boundaries.</strong> Use GitHub’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI usage guides"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI usage guides</a> </span> for the current invocation and control options. Define allowed tools, time limits, and output handling before running unattended jobs. Avoid converting an interactive permission policy into blanket authorization for a pipeline.</p> <h2 id="what-vs-code-adds"> <a href="#what-vs-code-adds" title="What VS Code Adds">What VS Code Adds</a> <a href="#what-vs-code-adds" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What VS Code Adds">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Copilot’s IDE experience includes suggestions, chat, and agentic tasks.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="IDE overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-in-ides"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-in-ides" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >IDE overview</a> </span> separates those functions. Inline assistance fits work where you remain the primary editor. Agent mode fits a bounded outcome requiring changes across files.</p> <p><strong>Agent mode edits and runs commands iteratively.</strong> GitHub’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Agent-mode guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-in-your-ide/use-copilot-agents/use-agent-mode?tool=vscode"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-in-your-ide/use-copilot-agents/use-agent-mode?tool=vscode" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Agent-mode guide</a> </span> describes selecting Agent in chat, reviewing changes, and extending tools through MCP. Availability and command approval behavior also depend on configuration and administration.</p> <p><strong>Evaluate context transfer deliberately.</strong> Select a function and ask for an explanation of its error handling. Then request a small change with an independent test. Record whether you needed to supply neighboring files or correct the agent’s assumption about the selected code.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/copilot-terminal-editor-bridge.webp", "caption": "Terminal prompt linked to an editor selection and side-by-side code diff within one repository workspace", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.444689241 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.410303930", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.444689241 +0000 UTC m=+546.410303930"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/copilot-terminal-editor-bridge.webp" alt="Terminal prompt linked to an editor selection and side-by-side code diff within one repository workspace"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>A connected CLI session combines terminal input with editor review</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="connect-the-two-interfaces"> <a href="#connect-the-two-interfaces" title="Connect the Two Interfaces">Connect the Two Interfaces</a> <a href="#connect-the-two-interfaces" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Connect the Two Interfaces">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>/ide </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Use <code>/ide</code> in an interactive Copilot CLI session</strong> to inspect or change the VS Code connection. GitHub’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="connection guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/connecting-vs-code"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/connecting-vs-code" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >connection guide</a> </span> documents matching a trusted workspace, sharing editor selection, and showing proposed file edits as diffs.</p> <p><strong>Automatic connection depends on the workspace match.</strong> A local CLI does not connect to a remote Codespace merely because its repository name matches. Run the CLI in the corresponding environment. Broad edit authorization also bypasses the proposed-edit diff approval flow, so check permissions if expected prompts disappear.</p> <p><strong>CLI transcripts are visible through VS Code’s Sessions view</strong>, with continuation through Resume in Terminal. This preserves the terminal workflow. Do not assume it converts the conversation into an interchangeable native editor-agent session.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Before connecting</th> <th>Verify</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Workspace</strong></td> <td>Intended folder is open and trusted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution location</strong></td> <td>CLI and editor integration refer to the same environment</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Selection</strong></td> <td>Highlighted code matches the current request</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Permissions</strong></td> <td>Proposed-edit review remains enabled if required</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Session</strong></td> <td>Continuing the intended conversation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="models-billing-and-policy"> <a href="#models-billing-and-policy" title="Models, Billing, and Policy">Models, Billing, and Policy</a> <a href="#models-billing-and-policy" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Models, Billing, and Policy">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use the same selected model for an interface trial where available.</strong> If the model choices differ, record the mismatch. A different model, context selection, or tool set changes the experiment beyond the graphical-versus-terminal distinction.</p> <p><strong>Verify current usage accounting in your account.</strong> GitHub’s Agent-mode documentation refers to AI Credits. Do not apply old premium-request estimates to a current account without checking its billing arrangement. A CLI prompt and an editor task are not automatically equivalent units of work.</p> <p><strong>Organization access is a prerequisite.</strong> If a feature is missing, check policy before reinstalling the extension. Record the approved tools and integrations for both surfaces. A provider login does not automatically grant authority to modify every repository or contact every external service.</p> <h2 id="run-a-paired-trial"> <a href="#run-a-paired-trial" title="Run a Paired Trial">Run a Paired Trial</a> <a href="#run-a-paired-trial" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Run a Paired Trial">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Prepare two copies of the same starting revision.</strong> Use matching instructions and acceptance tests. Keep the first attempt in the standalone CLI and the second in VS Code Agent mode. Run a third attempt with the connected CLI only if the mixed interaction suits your normal work.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Measure</th> <th>Reason to record it</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Context supplied</strong></td> <td>Reveals hidden manual setup effort</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Correctness</strong></td> <td>Distinguishes plausible code from a verified fix</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Approval steps</strong></td> <td>Shows the supervision burden under matching policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Review time</strong></td> <td>Measures effort to understand the whole patch</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Manual repairs</strong></td> <td>Captures work remaining after the agent finishes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Usage</strong></td> <td>Connects cost with accepted outcomes</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Keep recovery in the test.</strong> Reject one proposed approach and explain why. Observe whether the next attempt preserves useful work and respects the correction. This reveals more about daily usability than a single uninterrupted demo.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-next-steps"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">Troubleshooting and Next Steps</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>If the CLI connects to the wrong editor window</strong>, inspect <code>/ide</code> and select the intended workspace. If visual approval stops appearing, check broad edit permissions. If Agent mode is unavailable, inspect the extension state and organization policy.</p> <p><strong>Choose the standalone CLI</strong> when shell context and repeatable task invocation dominate. <strong>Choose VS Code</strong> when selection-based context, inline work, and graphical review dominate. <strong>Use the connected CLI</strong> when terminal task entry and editor inspection work well together.</p> <p><strong>For cross-vendor choices</strong>, read the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI master comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI master comparison</a> </span> or <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GUI master comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >GUI master comparison</a> </span> . Keep those evaluations separate from this same-family interface trial.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: GUI Coding Agents Compared: Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Copilot, and Continue
item.description: Compare graphical coding agents, separate full editors from extensions, and examine Roo Code shutdown context, model access, approvals, and review workflows.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Graphical coding agents</strong> put task conversations beside files, diffs, diagnostics, and application previews. This guide compares Cursor, the Windsurf/Cascade product line, Cline’s VS Code extension, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, and Continue’s IDE extension. Roo Code appears as a legacy migration consideration because its documentation now reports a shutdown.</p> <p><strong>Choose the workspace before the model.</strong> A standalone editor changes your development environment. An extension adds an agent to an existing editor. Evaluate both the generated patch and the effort required to inspect it.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Cursor and the Windsurf product line</strong> belong in the full-editor group.</li> <li><strong>Cline, Copilot, and Continue</strong> offer agent workflows inside an existing editor.</li> <li><strong>Roo Code needs migration planning</strong>, not treatment as a routine new deployment.</li> <li><strong>Visible changes still need tests</strong>, dependency review, and an explicit acceptance decision.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Scope and date:</strong> Official documentation checked on October 6, 2026. This is a workflow comparison, not a speed or coding-quality benchmark. Terminal products are covered separately in the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI comparison</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> An existing project, working tests, and permission to install the chosen editor or extension. Difficulty is beginner to intermediate. Allow an afternoon for two product trials.</p> <h2 id="current-names-and-status"> <a href="#current-names-and-status" title="Current Names and Status">Current Names and Status</a> <a href="#current-names-and-status" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Current Names and Status">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Windsurf’s Cascade documentation redirects to Devin Desktop.</strong> The current <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Cascade reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade"> <a href="https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Cascade reference</a> </span> places it inside Devin Desktop alongside another local agent. This article uses “Windsurf/Cascade” to connect the familiar name with the current documentation. Check the installed product and selected agent before reproducing an older tutorial.</p> <p><strong>Roo Code’s documentation reports an extension shutdown on 2026-05-15.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="official documentation notice"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/"> <a href="https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >official documentation notice</a> </span> points readers toward alternatives. Existing code or archived instructions do not establish ongoing maintenance. Exclude Roo from a new rollout unless you separately evaluate a maintained fork and its ownership, releases, and support.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Product surface</th> <th>Category</th> <th>Role in a shortlist</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Cursor editor</strong></td> <td>Full graphical editor</td> <td>Integrated agent and review workflow</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Windsurf/Cascade</strong></td> <td>Full graphical editor lineage</td> <td>Current Cascade workflow in Devin Desktop</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Cline in VS Code</strong></td> <td>Editor extension</td> <td>Provider choice and tool-driven tasks</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Copilot in VS Code</strong></td> <td>Editor integration</td> <td>Suggestions, chat, and agent work</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Continue extension</strong></td> <td>Editor extension</td> <td>Configurable models and task modes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Roo Code</strong></td> <td>Legacy extension</td> <td>Migration reference, not an active recommendation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="full-editors"> <a href="#full-editors" title="Full Editors">Full Editors</a> <a href="#full-editors" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Full Editors">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Cursor Agent</strong> combines instructions, tools, and the selected model. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="agent overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview"> <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >agent overview</a> </span> documents file changes, terminal execution, browser interaction, and checkpoints. Checkpoints are separate from Git, so use them for session recovery while keeping commits as the durable review record.</p> <p><strong>Cascade</strong> provides code and chat modes, editor-aware context, tool use, and checkpoints. The current documentation describes automatic inclusion of selected editor or terminal text. For an evaluation, record which context you supplied and which agent was active. Switching the surrounding editor or local agent changes the comparison.</p> <p><strong>A full-editor trial needs migration checks.</strong> Open your existing workspace and verify language support, formatting, debugging, keybindings, and extensions before measuring agent output. An agent saving time on patches does not compensate for a broken debugger in your daily workflow.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Editor test</th> <th>Evidence to collect</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Project startup</strong></td> <td>Existing build and launch tasks still work</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Language tooling</strong></td> <td>Diagnostics and navigation match your baseline</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Agent edits</strong></td> <td>Changes appear in a reviewable diff</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Undo preserves unrelated manual work</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Application checks</strong></td> <td>Tests and interactive behavior agree</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="extensions-in-your-editor"> <a href="#extensions-in-your-editor" title="Extensions in Your Editor">Extensions in Your Editor</a> <a href="#extensions-in-your-editor" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Extensions in Your Editor">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Cline’s VS Code extension</strong> reads and writes files, executes commands, and uses tools from the editor. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.cline.bot/cline-overview"> <a href="https://docs.cline.bot/cline-overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >overview</a> </span> describes several model-access routes, including provider credentials and local runtimes. This comparison evaluates the extension, even though Cline also ships other interfaces.</p> <p><strong>GitHub Copilot in VS Code</strong> includes suggestions, chat, and agentic changes. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="IDE overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-in-ides"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-in-ides" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >IDE overview</a> </span> separates these experiences. Evaluate inline assistance separately from delegated tasks, since accepting a completion and reviewing a multi-file change involve different decisions.</p> <p><strong>Continue’s extension</strong> separates Chat, Plan, and Agent modes. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Agent quick start"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.continue.dev/ide-extensions/agent/quick-start"> <a href="https://docs.continue.dev/ide-extensions/agent/quick-start" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Agent quick start</a> </span> explains read-only planning and tool-enabled implementation. It also identifies model/provider tool support as a prerequisite. A connected model is not sufficient evidence of a working agent configuration.</p> <p><strong>Extensions reduce editor migration work</strong>, but configuration still matters. Check conflicting shortcuts, language-server behavior, tool approvals, and the selected provider. Disable competing agent extensions during the initial trial so you know which integration produced each result.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/editor-extension-review-workflow.webp", "caption": "Full editor and extension layouts converging on a visual diff, diagnostics panel, and independent test checklist", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.448091038 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.413705727", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.448091038 +0000 UTC m=+546.413705727"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/editor-extension-review-workflow.webp" alt="Full editor and extension layouts converging on a visual diff, diagnostics panel, and independent test checklist"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Compare the effort needed to inspect and accept a change</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="review-and-control"> <a href="#review-and-control" title="Review and Control">Review and Control</a> <a href="#review-and-control" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Review and Control">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A useful GUI exposes the basis for a decision.</strong> Look for the changed files, command output, pending actions, and a clear way to redirect work. A polished chat panel alone provides little evidence about what happened to your repository.</p> <p><strong>Separate approval from final acceptance.</strong> Allowing a command lets the agent perform work. Accepting the final patch means you have reviewed scope and behavior. A sequence of individually approved operations still produces a combined diff requiring review.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Review question</th> <th>What to inspect</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>What changed?</strong></td> <td>Full diff, including configuration and lockfiles</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Why did it change?</strong></td> <td>Connection between the requirement and each edit</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What ran?</strong></td> <td>Commands, exit status, and useful output</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What failed?</strong></td> <td>Unresolved errors and abandoned approaches</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What is recoverable?</strong></td> <td>Checkpoint behavior and your Git baseline</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Use an existing uncommitted edit as a recovery test</strong> in a disposable copy of the project. Let the agent make a separate change, then undo its work. Verify your original edit survives. This tests an everyday workflow failure without risking your active checkout.</p> <h2 id="models-privacy-and-billing"> <a href="#models-privacy-and-billing" title="Models, Privacy, and Billing">Models, Privacy, and Billing</a> <a href="#models-privacy-and-billing" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Models, Privacy, and Billing">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>An editor window does not identify the inference destination.</strong> Record the selected model, provider account, repository indexing behavior, tool connections, and execution environment. A local extension and a local model are separate properties.</p> <p><strong>Keep pricing tied to the access route.</strong> Subscription allowances, hosted-service usage, and provider API billing are different arrangements. Check current product terms and your account dashboard instead of comparing an extension’s purchase price with another product’s inference allowance.</p> <p><strong>Team rollout adds another decision layer.</strong> Verify approved models, install/update policy, credential handling, repository exclusions, and support ownership. Document which settings users control and which administrators enforce. Avoid assuming one product’s policy options transfer to another extension.</p> <h2 id="a-practical-shortlist"> <a href="#a-practical-shortlist" title="A Practical Shortlist">A Practical Shortlist</a> <a href="#a-practical-shortlist" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="A Practical Shortlist">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Starting situation</th> <th>First comparison</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Willing to change editors</strong></td> <td>Cursor and the current Windsurf/Cascade workspace</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Keeping VS Code and Copilot access</strong></td> <td>Copilot Agent mode and Cline</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Choosing your own providers</strong></td> <td>Cline and Continue</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Migrating from Roo Code</strong></td> <td>Cline plus another currently maintained option</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Mostly writing code manually</strong></td> <td>Inline assistance first, delegated tasks second</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Run an editor-specific exercise.</strong> Select a failing function, ask for a diagnosis, approve a bounded fix, inspect the diff, and run independent tests. Then make a manual correction while the conversation remains open. Observe whether the next agent turn preserves it.</p> <p><strong>Score the whole interaction.</strong> Record task correctness, context supplied manually, approval interruptions, review effort, and recovery behavior. Do not turn visual polish or the number of available buttons into a coding-quality score.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-next-steps"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">Troubleshooting and Next Steps</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A disabled agent mode often needs a setup check.</strong> Confirm model tool support, workspace trust, organization policy, and extension compatibility before changing models at random. If editor diagnostics and command-line tests disagree, check interpreter selection and environment variables.</p> <p><strong>Choose one editor setup for a week</strong> after the initial trial and keep a small log of accepted changes and repairs. Use <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Copilot CLI vs VS Code"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/github-copilot-cli-vs-vscode/"> <a href="/articles/github-copilot-cli-vs-vscode/" rel="follow me" >Copilot CLI vs VS Code</a> </span> for GitHub’s cross-interface workflow, or compare <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Codex"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/codex-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/codex-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >Codex</a> </span> , <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Claude Code"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/claude-code-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/claude-code-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >Claude Code</a> </span> , and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/opencode-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/opencode-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >OpenCode</a> </span> within their own product families.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Local AI Coding on a 16GB GPU: Strata, OpenCode, and Qwen3.8
item.description: Run a local coding agent with Strata and OpenCode. Examine reported RTX 4060 Ti results, RAM requirements, prompt reuse, reasoning budgets, and the limits of replacing a paid subscription.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>A local coding agent on a 16GB GPU is a practical option for bounded development tasks.</strong> Strata and OpenCode combine local inference with file editing, shell commands, and test execution. A reported Qwen3.8-Flash-Next run on an RTX 4060 Ti completed an application, subsequent changes, and a racing-game prototype without paid inference calls.</p> <p><strong>Replacing a subscription requires a broader test.</strong> The published results demonstrate a working setup on one machine. They do not establish parity with paid coding services across languages, repositories, or difficult debugging tasks. The hardware also includes 64GB of system RAM, which carries much of the model.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>16GB describes GPU memory</strong>, not the total memory needed for the reported configuration.</li> <li><strong>Prompt reuse matters</strong> because coding agents repeatedly submit overlapping conversation history.</li> <li><strong>Reasoning needs a budget</strong> so planning leaves space for code and tool calls.</li> <li><strong>Passing generated tests is partial evidence</strong>, with Docker and gameplay requiring separate checks.</li> <li><strong>Zero API spend excludes ownership costs</strong>, electricity, and maintenance time.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> A compatible computer, enough free storage for the selected model, Git, Node.js with npm, and familiarity with terminal tools. Match the reported IQ3_S setup with 64GB of RAM. Use the current Strata installer to check other configurations.</p> <p><strong>Time and difficulty:</strong> Intermediate. Allow time for large model downloads and installation before evaluating task completion speed. The reported task timings exclude setup.</p> <h2 id="the-tested-configuration"> <a href="#the-tested-configuration" title="The Tested Configuration">The Tested Configuration</a> <a href="#the-tested-configuration" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The Tested Configuration">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Component</th> <th>Reported configuration</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>GPU</strong></td> <td>NVIDIA RTX 4060 Ti, 16GB VRAM</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>CPU</strong></td> <td>Intel Core i5-11600K</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>System memory</strong></td> <td>64GB RAM</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Storage</strong></td> <td>NVMe SSD</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Model</strong></td> <td>Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 125B MoE, IQ3_S</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Inference engine</strong></td> <td>Strata</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Coding agent</strong></td> <td>OpenCode</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Configured context</strong></td> <td>65,536 tokens</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Configured output limit</strong></td> <td>16,384 tokens</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>NetworkCoder’s published configuration and results</strong> supply these figures. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="test repository"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/network-tocoder/Free-Local-AI-Coding-Agent-125B-on-16GB-GPU"> <a href="https://github.com/network-tocoder/Free-Local-AI-Coding-Agent-125B-on-16GB-GPU" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >test repository</a> </span> reports loading 46.84GiB of expert weights in 28 seconds, with 4,431 experts occupying 8.45GiB of GPU memory. These measurements describe the tested run, not a guaranteed allocation on another engine version.</p> <p><strong>Current compatibility is broader than this test.</strong> As checked on October 6, 2026, the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Strata project"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata"> <a href="https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Strata project</a> </span> documents selected NVIDIA and AMD cards with at least 12GB of VRAM, plus smaller model options for 32GB RAM systems. Those options do not reproduce the 16GB GPU, 64GB RAM, IQ3_S experiment. Check the exact GPU, model variant, and runtime support before buying hardware.</p> <h2 id="where-the-model-lives"> <a href="#where-the-model-lives" title="Where the Model Lives">Where the Model Lives</a> <a href="#where-the-model-lives" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Where the Model Lives">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Mixture of experts</strong>, or MoE, activates a subset of a model’s expert networks for each token. This reduces the active computation compared with using every parameter on every step. The remaining weights still need storage and a route into computation.</p> <p><strong>Strata’s hybrid execution</strong> keeps frequently used experts on the GPU while retaining the expert collection in system RAM. The CPU computes uncached experts in place while the GPU handles cached experts. Storage also supports model files and lookup data. The system does not squeeze the entire 125B model into 16GB of VRAM.</p> <p><strong>GPU memory has competing uses.</strong> Runtime allocations, attention state, and the expert cache share a limited resource. More room for context changes the remaining expert-cache capacity. Current Strata versions also support KV-cache streaming, so the exact placement differs from an older configuration. Consult the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="technical documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/main/docs/DETAILS.md"> <a href="https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/main/docs/DETAILS.md" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >technical documentation</a> </span> for your engine version.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/local-agent-gpu-ram-expert-cache.webp", "caption": "Illustration of a local workstation distributing model execution across a graphics card, system memory, and solid-state storage", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.453071738 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.418686437", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.453071738 +0000 UTC m=+546.418686437"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/local-agent-gpu-ram-expert-cache.webp" alt="Illustration of a local workstation distributing model execution across a graphics card, system memory, and solid-state storage"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>The GPU is one part of the inference system, alongside CPU execution, system RAM, and storage</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="prompt-reuse-changes-speed"> <a href="#prompt-reuse-changes-speed" title="Prompt Reuse Changes Speed">Prompt Reuse Changes Speed</a> <a href="#prompt-reuse-changes-speed" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Prompt Reuse Changes Speed">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A coding agent runs a loop:</strong> read the task, request a tool action, receive its result, and decide the next action. File contents, errors, and test output accumulate in the conversation. Agents also compact or select context, so not every implementation resends an unchanged full history forever.</p> <p><strong>Prefill</strong> processes input tokens before generation. <strong>Decode</strong> produces the response. A system with fast decode but slow repeated prefill still leaves you waiting between tool calls.</p> <p><strong>The reported 44K-token timing used prefix reuse.</strong> Strata reused previously processed conversation content, with the growing prompt ready in roughly one to three seconds. This is useful evidence for a continuing agent session. It is not evidence of processing 44,000 entirely new tokens from scratch in one second.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Measurement</th> <th>What to record</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Cold prompt</strong></td> <td>Time for new content without reusable prefix state</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Warm continuation</strong></td> <td>Time after appending a tool result to existing context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Generation speed</strong></td> <td>Tokens per second during the response</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Task duration</strong></td> <td>Planning, generation, tools, tests, and retries together</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Two caches serve different purposes.</strong> The expert cache keeps frequently used weights near GPU computation. Prefix reuse avoids repeating work on earlier input. A high expert-cache hit rate does not prove a prompt-cache hit.</p> <h2 id="what-the-tasks-demonstrated"> <a href="#what-the-tasks-demonstrated" title="What the Tasks Demonstrated">What the Tasks Demonstrated</a> <a href="#what-the-tasks-demonstrated" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What the Tasks Demonstrated">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Task</th> <th>Reported time</th> <th>Reported outcome</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Build task manager</strong></td> <td>3m 38s</td> <td>Express API, interface, 5/5 tests</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Fix editing and add dates</strong></td> <td>4m 58s</td> <td>Changes completed, 6/6 tests</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Add export/import and packaging</strong></td> <td>3m 48s</td> <td>7/7 tests, Docker build unverified</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Racing game, first attempt</strong></td> <td>6m 35s</td> <td>Output exhausted during reasoning, no code</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Racing game, budgeted retry</strong></td> <td>4m 51s</td> <td>Game generated, JavaScript syntax checked</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="published results file"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/network-tocoder/Free-Local-AI-Coding-Agent-125B-on-16GB-GPU/main/results.csv"> <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/network-tocoder/Free-Local-AI-Coding-Agent-125B-on-16GB-GPU/main/results.csv" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >published results file</a> </span> </strong> records output speeds of 48–52 tokens per second for the first task, 40–43 for the second, and 37–44 for the third. “Up to 52” is a peak within these observations, not a sustained rate for every task.</p> <p><strong>The first three tasks extend one application.</strong> The 5/5, 6/6, and 7/7 counts describe successive test suites. Adding them does not establish 18 independent capabilities. Tests written by the same agent also need review for coverage and meaningful assertions.</p> <p><strong>Environmental recovery was part of the work.</strong> The agent recovered from an inappropriate shell command and identified a stale application server during testing. These are useful behaviors, though terminating an existing process deserves deliberate permissions in a shared development environment.</p> <p><strong>Docker remained unverified.</strong> The agent wrote a Dockerfile but lacked a running Docker engine for the build. Application tests passing outside the container do not establish a working image. The game retry likewise checked syntax and opened a browser, while the agent lacked direct visual confirmation of gameplay.</p> <h2 id="reserve-space-for-output"> <a href="#reserve-space-for-output" title="Reserve Space for Output">Reserve Space for Output</a> <a href="#reserve-space-for-output" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Reserve Space for Output">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span style="display:flex;"><span>{ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"reasoning_budget_tokens"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">8000</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Merge this setting into the existing <code>strata-iq3_s.json</code> configuration</strong>, preserving its other fields, then restart the selected Strata model. It is a Strata setting, not a replacement OpenCode configuration file. Verify the active budget in startup output.</p> <p><strong>Strata documents a hard reasoning budget</strong> which ends the thinking phase and transitions toward an answer. A request-level value overrides the configured default. The setting is different from a general reasoning-effort instruction such as low or high.</p> <p><strong>The first game attempt exhausted its 16,384-token allowance while planning.</strong> The retry applied an 8,000-token thinking budget and delivered code. This supports using a bounded reasoning phase for this workload. It does not establish 8,000 as the best setting for every task.</p> <p><strong>The remaining output allowance is a maximum, not a reservation guarantee.</strong> If an 8,000-token cap were fully consumed under a 16,384-token total limit, roughly 8,384 tokens would remain before other overhead. The result log reports 11,054 tokens written on the retry without a complete reasoning-versus-code breakdown. Do not interpret it as 8,000 reasoning tokens plus 11,054 code tokens under the same limit.</p> <p><strong>Use a smaller budget for narrow edits</strong>, then test larger budgets for tasks needing more analysis. Inspect complete file output, finish status, and test results. More planning time is useful only when it improves the delivered change.</p> <h2 id="connect-strata-and-opencode"> <a href="#connect-strata-and-opencode" title="Connect Strata and OpenCode">Connect Strata and OpenCode</a> <a href="#connect-strata-and-opencode" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Connect Strata and OpenCode">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>git clone https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata.git </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cd Strata </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>./setup.sh </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>This is the Linux setup entry point.</strong> Review the current installation instructions and use <strong><code>START-HERE.bat</code></strong> for the documented Windows path. Select the original Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S variant and a 65,536-token context to approximate the reported configuration. Save the engine version and selected model files with your benchmark notes.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>npm install -g opencode-ai </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Install OpenCode</strong> using its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="official instructions"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >official instructions</a> </span> . In a separate terminal, define <strong><code>STRATA_BASE_URL</code></strong> as the local API base printed by Strata, including its <strong><code>/v1</code></strong> suffix. Keep inference bound to the local machine for this setup.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span style="display:flex;"><span>{ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"provider"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"strata"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"npm"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"name"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"Strata local"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"options"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"baseURL"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"{env:STRATA_BASE_URL}"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"apiKey"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"local"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> }, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"models"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"name"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"limit"</span>: { <span style="color:#f92672">"context"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">65536</span>, <span style="color:#f92672">"output"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">16384</span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> }, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"model"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"strata/qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Merge the provider block into <code>~/.config/opencode/opencode.json</code></strong>, preserving existing settings. This adapts the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="published example configuration"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/network-tocoder/Free-Local-AI-Coding-Agent-125B-on-16GB-GPU/main/config/opencode.json"> <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/network-tocoder/Free-Local-AI-Coding-Agent-125B-on-16GB-GPU/main/config/opencode.json" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >published example configuration</a> </span> by loading the local endpoint from an environment variable. OpenCode documents <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="custom providers"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >custom providers</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="environment substitution"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/config/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/config/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >environment substitution</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong><code>local</code> is a placeholder credential</strong>, matching the example’s unauthenticated local setup. It does not secure a server. If your Strata instance enables authentication, supply its configured credential through the appropriate local secret mechanism.</p> <p><strong>Start <code>opencode</code> in a disposable project copy</strong> and select the configured model. Verify the selected provider before sending code. The client-side context declaration does not increase the server’s configured context, and a 65,536-token window does not leave 65,536 tokens for input when output space is also needed.</p> <h2 id="local-inference-and-permissions"> <a href="#local-inference-and-permissions" title="Local Inference and Permissions">Local Inference and Permissions</a> <a href="#local-inference-and-permissions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Local Inference and Permissions">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span style="display:flex;"><span>{ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"permission"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"edit"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"ask"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"bash"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"ask"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Merge these initial permissions into OpenCode’s configuration</strong> while evaluating the agent. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="permission documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >permission documentation</a> </span> explains the available controls. File changes and shell execution affect your machine regardless of where inference runs.</p> <p><strong>Local inference does not make every tool local.</strong> Package downloads, web tools, external integrations, and optional sharing still involve network services. Review enabled tools before handling private repositories. “The model runs locally” is a narrower claim than “nothing leaves the computer.”</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-the-first-run"> <a href="#troubleshooting-the-first-run" title="Troubleshooting the First Run">Troubleshooting the First Run</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-the-first-run" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting the First Run">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Symptom</th> <th>Check first</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Provider unavailable</strong></td> <td>Strata is running and the environment variable reaches the OpenCode process</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Model missing from selection</strong></td> <td>Provider ID and model ID match the saved configuration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Context-limit error</strong></td> <td>Prompt length plus requested output fits the server’s active window</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Planning without code</strong></td> <td>Reasoning budget, total output limit, and finish status</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Slow continuation</strong></td> <td>Prefix reuse, memory pressure, expert-cache behavior, and competing processes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Docker command fails</strong></td> <td>A functioning engine is available, rather than only its command-line client</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Change one setting at a time</strong> and repeat the same task from a saved starting state. This separates a configuration improvement from a different prompt or an easier test.</p> <h2 id="does-it-replace-a-subscription"> <a href="#does-it-replace-a-subscription" title="Does It Replace a Subscription?">Does It Replace a Subscription?</a> <a href="#does-it-replace-a-subscription" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Does It Replace a Subscription?">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Local setup is worth testing</th> <th>Keep another option available</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Existing compatible hardware</strong></td> <td>Purchasing hardware solely for an untested workload</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Bounded application changes</strong></td> <td>Large unfamiliar repositories and difficult migrations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Repeatable acceptance tests</strong></td> <td>Tasks without reliable ways to check correctness</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Time for runtime maintenance</strong></td> <td>Work requiring minimal setup and support overhead</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Zero API spend is meaningful</strong>, especially when hardware is already available. It excludes electricity, hardware depreciation, storage, and time spent maintaining the environment. The displayed zero-cost field also does not meter those expenses.</p> <p><strong>A subscription comparison needs matched tasks.</strong> Run the same starting repository, instructions, and acceptance checks through both systems. Record retries and human corrections alongside elapsed time. Include the failed first game attempt when evaluating the full workflow rather than reporting only the successful retry.</p> <p><strong>A useful local agent does not need universal superiority.</strong> If it reliably handles your routine edits and leaves a small set of difficult tasks for another tool, it already changes which paid services you need. Decide from accepted work on your own projects.</p> <h2 id="demonstration-and-next-steps"> <a href="#demonstration-and-next-steps" title="Demonstration and Next Steps">Demonstration and Next Steps</a> <a href="#demonstration-and-next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Demonstration and Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Local coding agent test with Strata, OpenCode, and a 16GB GPU"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/QBPbvMaHkJc/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QBPbvMaHkJc"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="QBPbvMaHkJc" videotitle="Local coding agent test with Strata, OpenCode, and a 16GB GPU" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QBPbvMaHkJc" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; The reported measurements above belong to the published test, not an independent benchmark performed for this article.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Reproduce one small task</strong> with fixed acceptance criteria and a saved starting revision.</li> <li><strong>Measure cold and warm turns</strong> instead of treating prefix reuse as cold prefill speed.</li> <li><strong>Verify packaging separately</strong> with a successful image build, startup, and container-level checks.</li> <li><strong>Inspect the generated tests</strong> and add cases the implementation did not anticipate.</li> <li><strong>Compare completed work</strong> against your current coding tool before changing subscriptions.</li> </ol> <p><strong>For hardware planning</strong>, read the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="local AI model and GPU context guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/"> <a href="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/" rel="follow me" >local AI model and GPU context guide</a> </span> . item.title: Local AI vs ChatGPT: How Close Are We Really?
item.description: Compare local AI with ChatGPT and Claude through benchmark scores, memory estimates, serving speed, and agent verification. Includes RTX 5090, DGX Spark, and Mac Studio scenarios.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Local AI</strong> is a practical option for bounded work with clear checks. Replacing the work you give ChatGPT or Claude requires three things to align: model capability, usable memory, and an agent equipped to inspect and verify its output.</p> <p>A model which fits your workstation still needs suitable tools and enough speed for repeated attempts. This article separates benchmark results, memory estimates, and completed-task evidence so you evaluate each on its own terms.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Capability:</strong> reference scores describe specific evaluation settings, not your local quantized build.</li> <li><strong>Memory:</strong> budget for weights, context cache, and runtime overhead together.</li> <li><strong>Speed:</strong> replaying an agent conversation measures serving performance, not correctness.</li> <li><strong>Verification:</strong> an agent needs checks matched to the requested result.</li> <li><strong>Selection:</strong> compare repeated tasks, repair time, and total cost before buying hardware.</li> </ul> <h2 id="read-scores-in-context"> <a href="#read-scores-in-context" title="Read Scores in Context">Read Scores in Context</a> <a href="#read-scores-in-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Read Scores in Context">#</a> </h2> <p>The <strong>Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index</strong> aggregates several evaluations into a reference score. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="model leaderboard"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models"> <a href="https://artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >model leaderboard</a> </span> and local hardware results show the following selected entries as checked on October 6, 2026.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model and setting</th> <th>Index score</th> <th>Deployment in this comparison</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Qwen3.8 27B, xhigh</strong></td> <td>34</td> <td>Downloadable weights</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>GLM-5.3, max</strong></td> <td>45</td> <td>Downloadable weights</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>GPT-6 Astra, max</strong></td> <td>53</td> <td>Hosted service</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Opus 5.5, max with fallback</strong></td> <td>58</td> <td>Hosted service</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Index points</strong> are not percentages of intelligence or task success. A 13-point gap between GLM and Claude does not establish a 13% difference in your coding results. Reasoning settings also matter when comparing entries for the same model.</p> <p>The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="published evaluation methodology"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking"> <a href="https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >published evaluation methodology</a> </span> describes the test setup. Some evaluations include tools and agent infrastructure. Treat the score as a result inside those conditions. Do not transfer it directly to a compressed local copy running through another application.</p> <p><strong>ChatGPT and Claude are products</strong>, while this table compares selected underlying models. Your subscription, selected model, available tools, and task context introduce additional differences. Start with a task you repeat, then test the complete setup.</p> <h2 id="budget-the-whole-request"> <a href="#budget-the-whole-request" title="Budget the Whole Request">Budget the Whole Request</a> <a href="#budget-the-whole-request" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Budget the Whole Request">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Memory fit</strong> starts with three allocations. Model weights store learned parameters. The key-value cache, or <strong>KV cache</strong>, retains attention data used during inference. Runtime buffers and other software consume the remaining space.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Required memory = resident weights + context cache + runtime allowance </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Available memory = physical capacity - operating system and application reserve </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Quantization</strong> reduces the storage precision of model weights. Lower precision reduces memory requirements, with quality dependent on the model and quantized build. Cache precision is a separate setting. A Q4 weight file does not establish a four-bit cache.</p> <p>For a rough weights-only example, 27 billion parameters at 16 bits require about 50.3 GiB. Eight bits gives about 25.1 GiB, and four bits gives about 12.6 GiB. <strong>Published file sizes</strong> also reflect metadata, packing, and mixed precision, so use the exact files for deployment planning.</p> <p>The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Qwen3.8-27B model card"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Qwen3.8-27B model card</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GLM-5.3 model card"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >GLM-5.3 model card</a> </span> describe different architectures. A <strong>mixture-of-experts model</strong> activates only part of its parameters for each token, but the remaining weights still require storage. Offloading changes placement and latency, rather than eliminating those weights.</p> <h2 id="start-with-published-files"> <a href="#start-with-published-files" title="Start With Published Files">Start With Published Files</a> <a href="#start-with-published-files" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Start With Published Files">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Download size</strong> gives a more concrete starting point than parameter count.
