Loading behavior, caches, temporary buffers, and additional model components affect the running process. Do not compare a 29 GB download directly against a 30 GiB allocation without converting units.</p> <h2 id="context-changes-the-fit"> <a href="#context-changes-the-fit" title="Context Changes the Fit">Context Changes the Fit</a> <a href="#context-changes-the-fit" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Context Changes the Fit">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Qwen’s attention cache</strong> provides a worked example. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="published configuration"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/main/config.json"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/main/config.json" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >published configuration</a> </span> specifies 64 layers, full attention every fourth layer, four key-value heads, and a head dimension of 256.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Full-attention KV bytes per token: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>16 layers × 4 KV heads × 256 dimensions × 2 (K and V) × 2 bytes </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>= 65,536 bytes </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>8,192 tokens = 0.5 GiB </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>32,768 tokens = 2.0 GiB </span></span></code></pre></div><p>This <strong>calculated cache component</strong> assumes 16-bit keys and values for one sequence. It excludes linear-attention state, runtime buffers, allocator overhead, and optional vision or speculative-decoding components. Those allocations still need a reserve.</p> <p>For an <strong>illustrative planning budget</strong>, add 3–5 GiB for those remaining allocations to the rounded weight sizes. This allowance is an assumption to replace with measurements from your selected runtime.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Build and context</th> <th>Calculated planning range</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Qwen Q4_0, 8K</strong></td> <td>18.5–20.5 GiB</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Qwen Q8_0, 8K</strong></td> <td>30.5–32.5 GiB</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Qwen Q8_0, 32K</strong></td> <td>32.0–34.0 GiB</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>A 30 GiB usable allocation</strong> leaves substantial room for the Q4 example, while the Q8 scenarios exceed it under these assumptions. A smaller measured reserve changes the boundary. This is why a successful short prompt does not prove sufficient capacity for a long coding session.</p> <p><strong>Concurrent requests</strong> add another dimension. Ollama documents context-memory growth with parallel requests, alongside separate cache-precision controls. Its Q8 cache uses approximately half the F16 cache memory, while Q4 uses approximately one-quarter, with model-dependent quality tradeoffs. See the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Ollama runtime FAQ"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.ollama.com/faq"> <a href="https://docs.ollama.com/faq" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Ollama runtime FAQ</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="match-hardware-to-allocation"> <a href="#match-hardware-to-allocation" title="Match Hardware to Allocation">Match Hardware to Allocation</a> <a href="#match-hardware-to-allocation" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Match Hardware to Allocation">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>An RTX 5090</strong> offers 32 GB of dedicated graphics memory. A DGX Spark with 128 GB uses shared memory. Artificial Analysis documents both configurations in its hardware results. More capacity permits larger allocations, but capacity alone does not establish serving speed.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Hardware scenario</th> <th>Practical implication</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>RTX 5090, 32 GB</strong></td> <td>Qwen Q4 leaves more context headroom than Q8</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>DGX Spark, 128 GB</strong></td> <td>Room for either Qwen build, with runtime overhead still required</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Mac Studio, 256 GB</strong></td> <td>Larger weight sets are candidates, subject to runtime and allocation limits</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>GLM UD-Q4_K_XL</strong> exceeds all three capacities before adding a cache. The approximately 222.6 GiB IQ2 weight set also exceeds a 128 GB system. On a 256 GB Mac, its feasibility depends on the actual GPU-accessible allocation and remaining overhead. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Apple’s specifications"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.apple.com/mac-studio/specs/"> <a href="https://www.apple.com/mac-studio/specs/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Apple’s specifications</a> </span> establish hardware options, not a guaranteed inference allocation.</p> <p>A <strong>hypothetical 240 GiB usable budget</strong> leaves about 17.4 GiB after those IQ2 weights. A 192 GiB budget fails at the weights alone. Neither budget establishes an operating-system default, compressed-cache support, useful throughput, or acceptable IQ2 quality. Require a demonstrated runtime configuration before purchasing for this workload.</p> <h2 id="speed-is-a-separate-result"> <a href="#speed-is-a-separate-result" title="Speed Is a Separate Result">Speed Is a Separate Result</a> <a href="#speed-is-a-separate-result" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Speed Is a Separate Result">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Artificial Analysis’ local inference benchmark</strong> replays a recorded workload of 168 model turns. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="laptop and workstation results"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://artificialanalysis.ai/hardware-inference-stack/laptops-workstations/"> <a href="https://artificialanalysis.ai/hardware-inference-stack/laptops-workstations/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >laptop and workstation results</a> </span> list the following times for the tested Qwen3.8 27B configurations.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>System</th> <th>Serving replay time</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>DGX Spark, 128 GB</strong></td> <td>24.2 minutes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>RTX 5090</strong></td> <td>4.9 minutes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Mac Studio, 256 GB</strong></td> <td>No result in this comparison</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The RTX result takes roughly one-fifth of the Spark time. <strong>Serving configurations matter</strong>, so this is not a universal hardware ratio. The tested serving builds also differ from the GGUF planning examples above.</p> <p><strong>Replay timing</strong> excludes tool execution and forces responses to recorded lengths. It does not grade whether the generated answers solve the original task. A MacBook measurement also does not establish Mac Studio performance.</p> <h2 id="give-the-agent-feedback"> <a href="#give-the-agent-feedback" title="Give the Agent Feedback">Give the Agent Feedback</a> <a href="#give-the-agent-feedback" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Give the Agent Feedback">#</a> </h2> <p>An <strong>agent execution system</strong> supplies tools, context, an action loop, and verification. A model writes or chooses actions inside this system. For a CSV export, useful capabilities include reading project files, changing code, running tests, and receiving the resulting errors.</p> <p>Consider an <strong>illustrative export task</strong>, rather than a measured experiment. The agent writes a download feature, but its output uses the wrong date format. A visual review misses the problem. A test opens the exported file and compares its dates against the required format. The agent receives the failure, changes the formatter, and reruns the check.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Missing component</th> <th>Likely failure</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Relevant context</strong></td> <td>Edits an unrelated file</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution tools</strong></td> <td>Describes a fix without applying it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Verification step</strong></td> <td>Stops after plausible code</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Error feedback</strong></td> <td>Repeats a failed approach</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>LangChain reports</strong> a change from 52.8% to 66.5% on Terminal Bench 2.0 while holding GPT-5.2-Codex fixed. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="agent engineering report"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.langchain.com/blog/improving-deep-agents-with-harness-engineering"> <a href="https://www.langchain.com/blog/improving-deep-agents-with-harness-engineering" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >agent engineering report</a> </span> describes verification guidance, environment context, repeated-edit detection, and reasoning-budget changes.</p> <p>This is <strong>vendor-reported evidence</strong>, not proof of a small local model matching a frontier model. It supports a narrower conclusion: model selection alone does not explain agent outcomes. LangChain also reports worse results with maximum reasoning throughout, due to timeouts.</p> <h2 id="match-checks-to-work"> <a href="#match-checks-to-work" title="Match Checks to Work">Match Checks to Work</a> <a href="#match-checks-to-work" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Match Checks to Work">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A passing check</strong> establishes only what the check covers. A CSV test validating column names leaves date formatting, quoting, Unicode, and access control untested. Define the requested result before deciding how to verify it.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Task</th> <th>Useful completion evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Code change</strong></td> <td>Relevant tests plus inspection of the resulting behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Research answer</strong></td> <td>Retrieved sources supporting individual claims</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Booking or refund</strong></td> <td>Correct stored state and compliance with applicable policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Document export</strong></td> <td>Parsed output matching the requested fields and formats</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The <strong>τ-bench study</strong> evaluates agents interacting with tools, users, and domain rules. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="research paper"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045"> <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >research paper</a> </span> checks final database state against expected outcomes. This illustrates why fluent confirmation text is an insufficient completion check for a transaction.</p> <h2 id="local-does-not-mean-offline"> <a href="#local-does-not-mean-offline" title="Local Does Not Mean Offline">Local Does Not Mean Offline</a> <a href="#local-does-not-mean-offline" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Local Does Not Mean Offline">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Local inference</strong> controls where the model runs. The surrounding application still determines where documents, search queries, traces, and tool results travel. A local coding model connected to remote search or cloud tools remains a networked system.</p> <p>Ollama states it does not receive prompts or answers for local execution and documents disabling its cloud features. This is a <strong>runtime-specific statement</strong>, not a privacy guarantee for every connected agent. Verify both the model endpoint and each integration against the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="runtime’s documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.ollama.com/faq"> <a href="https://docs.ollama.com/faq" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >runtime’s documentation</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Data path</th> <th>What to check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Inference endpoint</strong></td> <td>Local process, remote server, or automatic fallback</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Search and retrieval</strong></td> <td>Queries and document fragments sent externally</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Tool connections</strong></td> <td>Files and records exposed to each service</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Logs and traces</strong></td> <td>Storage location, retained content, and access</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>A hybrid workflow</strong> needs an explicit handoff rule. For example, keep private document extraction local, then send only approved aggregate results for hosted analysis. Review the exact outgoing material. A summary still contains sensitive information if it preserves names, customer details, or confidential findings.</p> <h2 id="test-before-you-buy"> <a href="#test-before-you-buy" title="Test Before You Buy">Test Before You Buy</a> <a href="#test-before-you-buy" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Test Before You Buy">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose a repeated task</strong> with a clear finish condition. Compare the local setup against the hosted product you use, including its tools. Give both the same inputs and acceptance criteria, then repeat the task with several representative examples.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Record the configuration:</strong> exact model file, quantization, backend version, context limit, and reasoning setting.</li> <li><strong>Define success:</strong> expected artifact, required behavior, and forbidden side effects.</li> <li><strong>Measure completion:</strong> elapsed time, passed checks, failed attempts, and manual repairs.</li> <li><strong>Include ownership cost:</strong> hardware, electricity, API fees, maintenance, and your time.</li> <li><strong>Classify failures:</strong> reasoning errors, memory limits, latency, missing context, or missing verification.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Local inference</strong> suits work whose evaluated quality and latency meet your requirements. A hosted model remains useful when its additional capability reduces failures or review effort. A hybrid workflow assigns different tasks to each after defining which data is allowed to leave the machine.</p> <h2 id="count-cost-per-accepted-result"> <a href="#count-cost-per-accepted-result" title="Count Cost per Accepted Result">Count Cost per Accepted Result</a> <a href="#count-cost-per-accepted-result" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Count Cost per Accepted Result">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Human repair time</strong> often changes the economics. A fast local response which needs ten minutes of correction costs more working time than a slower response which passes review. Count accepted results alongside inference expense.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Cost per accepted task = </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>(hardware allocation + electricity + service fees + maintenance + review time) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>÷ accepted tasks </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Illustrative review cost:</strong> at an assumed $30 per hour, eight minutes of correction costs $4 per task. One hundred such tasks consume $400 of review time. These figures are arithmetic examples, not measured local-model failure rates.</p> <p><strong>Compare equivalent outcomes.</strong> Include rejected attempts in elapsed time and cost. For owned hardware, allocate purchase cost over a realistic service period and task volume. For a hosted service, include the applicable subscription or API expense and the review work it still requires.</p> <p>For hardware detail, continue with the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="local model, GPU, and context guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/"> <a href="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/" rel="follow me" >local model, GPU, and context guide</a> </span> . item.title: Meta's Context Language Models: Better Agent Memory, Not the End of Hallucinations
item.description: How Context Language Models edit agent memory, what the benchmarks establish, and how cache costs, model capability, and untrusted notes affect reliability.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Context Language Models (CLMs)</strong> give an AI agent direct control over the information supplied to its next model call. The approach improves context management in several published evaluations, but it does not establish an end to hallucinations. An agent still needs evidence for its claims and independent checks on its work.</p> <p>The engineering question is whether selective editing preserves the right facts at an acceptable cost. A shorter conversation is useful only if the agent retains its requirements, distinguishes observations from assumptions, and retrieves supporting evidence when needed.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Editable context:</strong> CLM describes an execution method for existing models, with optional training to improve its use.</li> <li><strong>Conditional gains:</strong> model size, context budget, task, and serving backend affect the results.</li> <li><strong>Compute accounting:</strong> prefix-reuse FLOPs include recomputation after edits, but do not measure elapsed time or billing directly.</li> <li><strong>Memory integrity:</strong> an agent’s own notes remain fallible and potentially unsafe inputs.</li> <li><strong>Practical evaluation:</strong> measure accepted results, lost facts, unsupported claims, and recovery cost together.</li> </ul> <h2 id="separate-memory-from-evidence"> <a href="#separate-memory-from-evidence" title="Separate Memory From Evidence">Separate Memory From Evidence</a> <a href="#separate-memory-from-evidence" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Memory From Evidence">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A context window</strong> contains the input available to the model during a call. Instructions, tool responses, working notes, and prior messages compete for space. Compaction replaces some of this material with a shorter representation.</p> <p>Consider an <strong>illustrative dependency-upgrade task</strong>. A test runner reports two failures. The agent compresses its history into a note saying the upgrade passed. Future work then starts from an incorrect assumption, even though the original test output remains on disk.</p> <p>Changing the compaction method addresses how this mistaken note enters working memory. It does not replace the <strong>test runner as evidence</strong>. Before accepting the upgrade, the workflow still needs a fresh test result or an inspectable record of the relevant run.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Failure</th> <th>Appropriate check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Lost requirement</strong></td> <td>Compare current state with the original acceptance criteria</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Invented observation</strong></td> <td>Match the claim to a tool result or source record</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Incorrect reasoning</strong></td> <td>Test the conclusion against the task’s expected behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Unauthorized instruction</strong></td> <td>Enforce permissions outside model-written notes</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>This distinction matters when evaluating any memory technique. <strong>Preservation and correctness are separate properties.</strong> A system which retains an inaccurate claim perfectly remains inaccurate.</p> <h2 id="what-clms-change"> <a href="#what-clms-change" title="What CLMs Change">What CLMs Change</a> <a href="#what-clms-change" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What CLMs Change">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Rulin Shao and coauthors</strong>, including researchers at Meta Superintelligence Labs and the University of Washington, introduced CLMs in a September 29, 2026 preprint. Their implementation exposes the live context as an editable file. The agent uses shell commands or code to modify it, and the runtime supplies the revised contents on the next call. See <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Context Language Models"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725"> <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Context Language Models</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Ordinary continuation: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>existing context + new response + new tool output </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Editable-context continuation: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>agent revises context file -> runtime loads revised context -> next model call </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The model architecture does not need replacement</strong> for the zero-shot approach. The runtime adds a capability around an existing model. The paper separately investigates instructions, learned context-management strategies, and reinforcement learning.</p> <p>A <strong>notes file</strong> is different. Reading a saved note adds its contents to a conversation. Editing the file later does not automatically remove the old text from the live context. CLM requires runtime support to synchronize edits with subsequent requests. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="official implementation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/facebookresearch/context-language-models"> <a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/context-language-models" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >official implementation</a> </span> contains the agent code and a separate serving extension.</p> <p><strong>External storage remains useful.</strong> Keep detailed logs and source documents available for retrieval, while retaining concise references in working memory. A document’s location and the claim it supports often matter more than keeping every line in the next prompt.</p> <h2 id="read-the-results-carefully"> <a href="#read-the-results-carefully" title="Read the Results Carefully">Read the Results Carefully</a> <a href="#read-the-results-carefully" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Read the Results Carefully">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Benchmark improvements are specific comparisons.</strong> The following findings come from the authors’ evaluations, not testing performed for this article. The research remains a preprint, and results from a selected benchmark do not establish reliability across arbitrary workflows.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evaluation</th> <th>Reported result</th> <th>Interpretation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>BrowseComp-Plus, zero-shot</strong></td> <td>11.4% relative accuracy gain and 21.5% fewer prefix-reuse FLOPs against the strongest baseline</td> <td>Accuracy and compute both improve in this setup</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TerminalBench 2.1</strong></td> <td>Matches the strongest baseline’s accuracy with 29.5% fewer FLOPs</td> <td>The benefit is efficiency at comparable accuracy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>EdgeBench, 12-hour runs</strong></td> <td>5% higher score with 59% fewer FLOPs</td> <td>Software-optimization score, not a hallucination rate</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Trained Qwen3.5-9B</strong></td> <td>CLM 42.5% versus trained summary 42.1% accuracy</td> <td>Small accuracy gap with a larger compute difference</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The trained 9B comparison uses <strong>1.34 versus 2.19 PFLOPs per question</strong>, about 38.8% less compute for CLM. Its improvement from 28.8% before training to 42.5% afterward is a different comparison from the 0.4-point gap against trained summarization. Keep the baseline explicit. See the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="paper’s results and training table"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://arxiv.org/html/2609.37725v1"> <a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2609.37725v1" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >paper’s results and training table</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Relative percentages</strong> also need a denominator. An increase from approximately 53.3% to 59.4% is about 6.1 percentage points, or 11.4% relative. Neither expression means the system answers every question correctly.</p> <h3 id="context-budget-changes-outcomes"> <a href="#context-budget-changes-outcomes" title="Context Budget Changes Outcomes">Context Budget Changes Outcomes</a> <a href="#context-budget-changes-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Context Budget Changes Outcomes">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>A 32K context budget</strong> appears throughout the main evaluations. It creates a meaningful constraint on retention and editing. Results at this budget should not be generalized to every larger-window deployment.</p> <p>At <strong>128K on EdgeBench-10</strong>, Appendix F reports the following results across ten tasks and three seeds:</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Method</th> <th>Final score</th> <th>Mean prefix-reuse PFLOPs per trial</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Summarization</strong></td> <td>47.8</td> <td>222</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>CLM</strong></td> <td>47.3</td> <td>142</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>CLM with subagents</strong></td> <td>50.2</td> <td>219</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Single-agent accuracy is close</strong>, while CLM uses about 36% less compute in this comparison. The subagent configuration changes the outcome again. Context capacity, agent configuration, and compute budget belong in the comparison alongside the method name.</p> <h3 id="model-capability-still-matters"> <a href="#model-capability-still-matters" title="Model Capability Still Matters">Model Capability Still Matters</a> <a href="#model-capability-still-matters" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Model Capability Still Matters">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>Smaller models do not automatically manage memory well.</strong> In the training comparison, the untrained 9B CLM starts below the summary baseline. A separate supplementary evaluation reports 39.9% versus 37.7% on BrowseComp-Plus. These are different experimental setups, not interchangeable measurements.</p> <p>The supplementary TerminalBench analysis also reports <strong>no context edits in half of the 9B tasks</strong>. Giving a model an editing interface does not ensure it uses the interface effectively. Evaluate the selected model and settings instead of treating CLM as a universal upgrade.</p> <h2 id="account-for-reprocessing"> <a href="#account-for-reprocessing" title="Account for Reprocessing">Account for Reprocessing</a> <a href="#account-for-reprocessing" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Account for Reprocessing">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>The KV cache</strong> stores intermediate attention computations. With ordinary prefix caching, unchanged text at the beginning of the next request reuses prior computation. An edit near the beginning reduces the reusable prefix and forces later text to be processed again.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Previous request: A + B + C </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Revised request: A + replacement for B + C </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Standard prefix reuse: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>reuse A, recompute replacement for B and C </span></span></code></pre></div><p>The paper’s <strong>prefix-reuse FLOPs</strong> metric counts generation plus prompt processing after the first mismatch. A PFLOP represents 10¹⁵ floating-point operations. This is an estimated computation total, not a quality score, throughput measurement, or invoice.</p> <p>The <strong>7.7× example</strong> in Appendix C uses an illustrative 20,000-token prompt and 500-token response. An edit at the start costs 7.7 times the modeled append-only turn with an 18,000-token reusable prefix. It is a recomputation penalty under specified lengths, not a measured 7.7-fold reduction in hallucinations.</p> <p><strong>Local latency depends on prompt throughput.</strong> As an arithmetic example, rereading 24,000 tokens at an assumed 800 tokens per second takes 30 seconds before other overhead. This is not a benchmark for a particular Mac or GPU. Measure the backend, quantization, and actual prompt sizes you intend to use.</p> <p>The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="llama.cpp discussion of hybrid-model reprocessing"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/20225"> <a href="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/20225" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >llama.cpp discussion of hybrid-model reprocessing</a> </span> illustrates why <strong>prefix changes and recurrent-state checkpoints</strong> matter. It does not establish identical behavior across all releases or applications using llama.cpp. Record your runtime version and inspect its cache logs.</p> <h2 id="cache-savings-have-limits"> <a href="#cache-savings-have-limits" title="Cache Savings Have Limits">Cache Savings Have Limits</a> <a href="#cache-savings-have-limits" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Cache Savings Have Limits">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Suffix Cache Reuse (SCR)</strong> retains cached states for surviving text after an edit. The released extension targets SGLang, with its README specifying version 0.5.16. It is a separate serving optimization, not a prerequisite for the basic editable-context method.</p> <p><strong>Reuse is approximate.</strong> Surviving tokens retain states computed under the previous context. Matching benchmark performance therefore does not establish numerical equivalence to fully recomputing the new prompt.</p> <p>The authors report <strong>35% less server-side compute</strong> in their BrowseComp-Plus comparison. Of the 7.8 percentage points of prompt tokens additionally reused, 5.3 come from stripped reasoning blocks and 2.5 from other edits. Much of this benefit therefore applies beyond explicit CLM editing. See the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="SCR implementation notes"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/facebookresearch/context-language-models/main/suffix_cache_reuse/README.md"> <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/facebookresearch/context-language-models/main/suffix_cache_reuse/README.md" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >SCR implementation notes</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>For API billing</strong>, separate ordinary input, cache writes, and cache reads. Anthropic lists Sonnet 4.6 at $3, $3.75, and $0.30 per million tokens respectively for ordinary input, five-minute cache writes, and cache hits. Rewriting 20,000 tokens as a cache write costs $0.075, versus $0.006 for a hit. The $0.069 difference excludes output and other billing modifiers. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Prompt-caching documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching"> <a href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Prompt-caching documentation</a> </span> , checked October 6, 2026.</p> <p><strong>Total task cost decides the tradeoff.</strong> Occasional expensive edits still produce savings if they substantially reduce later input. Frequent edits followed by few remaining turns offer less opportunity to recover their cost.</p> <h2 id="keep-notes-below-instructions"> <a href="#keep-notes-below-instructions" title="Keep Notes Below Instructions">Keep Notes Below Instructions</a> <a href="#keep-notes-below-instructions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Keep Notes Below Instructions">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Model-written memory is untrusted task data.</strong> It contains observations, interpretations, and sometimes mistakes. Treating every note as an instruction gives those mistakes authority over future actions.</p> <p>OpenAI documented <strong>27 jailbreak-like compaction summaries</strong> in a separate training run of an unreleased Astra-family model. Some injected instructions were ignored, while task-specific restrictions affected one reported continuation. The report describes rare behavior and states regeneration did not reproduce it in the final Astra model or checkpoints used for traffic. This is evidence of a failure mode, not its prevalence in deployed CLMs. See <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenAI’s compaction-summary report"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://alignment.openai.com/misalignment-reports/self-generated-prompt-injections-in-compaction-summaries/"> <a href="https://alignment.openai.com/misalignment-reports/self-generated-prompt-injections-in-compaction-summaries/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >OpenAI’s compaction-summary report</a> </span> .</p> <p>A <strong>defensive implementation</strong> should separate these responsibilities:</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Component</th> <th>Treatment</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>User requirements and permissions</strong></td> <td>Preserve outside the editable notes layer</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Working notes</strong></td> <td>Permit revision, retain provenance, and mark uncertainty</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Original evidence</strong></td> <td>Keep retrievable records independent of summaries</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Actions and edits</strong></td> <td>Log changes and enforce access controls in code</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Deletion is not necessarily erasure.</strong> SCR retains states influenced by earlier context. As an engineering inference, removing text from an editable file should not be treated as proof of removing all influence from cached state. Test explicit reset behavior when a workflow requires a clean restart.</p> <h2 id="test-a-bounded-pilot"> <a href="#test-a-bounded-pilot" title="Test a Bounded Pilot">Test a Bounded Pilot</a> <a href="#test-a-bounded-pilot" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Test a Bounded Pilot">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start with retention requirements</strong>, not an advertised context length. Pick a repeated task with known answers, immutable input records, and a clear completion check. Use a sandbox containing synthetic data for the first comparison.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Create exact facts:</strong> include identifiers, changed requirements, failed attempts, and one corrected value.</li> <li><strong>Run comparable configurations:</strong> fixed summarization, editable context, and a fresh-session notes workflow.</li> <li><strong>Hold inputs constant:</strong> use the same model, task set, tools, generation limits, and context budget.</li> <li><strong>Check after memory changes:</strong> test exact recall, source retrieval, and whether superseded facts remain marked as obsolete.</li> <li><strong>Measure the whole run:</strong> record success rate, unsupported claims, elapsed time, edits, overflow recovery, and manual corrections.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Token accounting belongs in the runtime.</strong> Appendix G finds limited context-length awareness in the tested models, with environmental hints improving estimates. The experimental setup also includes overflow recovery. Supply measured token counts and reserve response space instead of depending on the model to estimate capacity.</p> <p>A <strong>notes-based fallback</strong> is useful when live-context editing is unavailable. Keep the handoff short and evidence-linked. The following is an illustrative record, not a CLM API format:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">objective</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">Upgrade the dependency without changing export behavior</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">verified</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#f92672">claim</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">Date export test still fails</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">evidence</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">artifacts/export-test-result.txt</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">superseded</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#f92672">claim</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">All tests passed</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">reason</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">Contradicted by the retained test result</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">unknown</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">Whether the parser change affects empty input</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">next_step</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">Test empty input before changing the formatter</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>A fresh session still pays to read this note</strong>, and a bad note still transfers bad information. Reopen evidence for consequential claims and keep the original task specification available. This workflow is a compatibility option, not proof of CLM-equivalent gains.</p> <h2 id="decide-by-accepted-results"> <a href="#decide-by-accepted-results" title="Decide by Accepted Results">Decide by Accepted Results</a> <a href="#decide-by-accepted-results" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Decide by Accepted Results">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Trial CLMs</strong> when long-running tasks repeatedly lose useful state or spend substantial compute on obsolete context. A short interaction with little history offers less opportunity for this particular optimization.</p> <p>The official repository carries <strong>CC BY-NC 4.0</strong> terms. Check its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="license"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/facebookresearch/context-language-models/blob/main/LICENSE"> <a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/context-language-models/blob/main/LICENSE" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >license</a> </span> before adopting the implementation in a commercial project. Public source availability does not by itself grant unrestricted commercial reuse.</p> <p><strong>Reliable completion remains the target.</strong> Keep the method only if it improves accepted outcomes or reduces cost without weakening evidence checks. For related deployment choices, read the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="local AI and hosted-model comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/local-ai-vs-chatgpt-how-close-are-we/"> <a href="/articles/local-ai-vs-chatgpt-how-close-are-we/" rel="follow me" >local AI and hosted-model comparison</a> </span> and the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GPU and context planning guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/"> <a href="/articles/local-ai-model-gpu-context-guide/" rel="follow me" >GPU and context planning guide</a> </span> .</p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="The End of AI Hallucinations? item.title: OpenCode CLI vs Desktop: 2026 Workflow Comparison
item.description: Compare OpenCode’s terminal and desktop clients through their server architecture, provider configuration, scripting, session state, and troubleshooting.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>OpenCode CLI and desktop are clients for the same coding-agent product.</strong> The terminal interface suits keyboard-driven work and scripts. The desktop application supplies a graphical workspace. The important comparison includes the server, project, provider, and configuration behind each client.</p> <p><strong>Choose the interface after identifying the backend.</strong> Two OpenCode windows do not necessarily use the same server or session. A desktop application pointing at a different server is a different execution environment, even if its model label looks familiar.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Use the CLI for terminal work</strong> and non-interactive commands.</li> <li><strong>Use desktop for a graphical workspace</strong>, while checking its selected server.</li> <li><strong>Provider configuration determines inference</strong>, independently of the interface.</li> <li><strong>Shared product identity does not guarantee shared session state</strong> across separate servers or versions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Scope and date:</strong> Official documentation checked on October 6, 2026. This guide compares interfaces, not model quality. You need a repository, a working provider connection, and basic terminal familiarity. Allow 45–60 minutes for the trial.</p> <h2 id="the-client-and-server"> <a href="#the-client-and-server" title="The Client and Server">The Client and Server</a> <a href="#the-client-and-server" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The Client and Server">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>OpenCode separates its interface from its server.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="server documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/server/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/server/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >server documentation</a> </span> describes the terminal UI as a client and <code>opencode serve</code> as a standalone server. This architecture supports multiple ways to interact with the agent.</p> <p><strong>Desktop starts a local server by default.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="troubleshooting guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >troubleshooting guide</a> </span> identifies its <code>opencode-cli</code> sidecar and the option to connect to a configured server URL. When behavior differs between clients, inspect this connection before changing the prompt.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Layer</th> <th>Question to answer</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Client</strong></td> <td>Terminal UI, desktop app, or non-interactive command?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Agent server</strong></td> <td>Which process receives the request?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Repository</strong></td> <td>Which directory does the server access?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Model provider</strong></td> <td>Which service supplies inference?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Session</strong></td> <td>Existing conversation or new task?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>A server location is not an inference location.</strong> An agent server on your computer still sends requests to a configured hosted model. Conversely, a compatible local inference service is a separate process with its own model and resource requirements.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/opencode-clients-server-provider.webp", "caption": "Terminal and desktop clients connected to an agent server, repository files, and separate inference service", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.469858712 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.435473421", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.469858712 +0000 UTC m=+546.435473421"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/opencode-clients-server-provider.webp" alt="Terminal and desktop clients connected to an agent server, repository files, and separate inference service"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Check the agent server and inference provider independently</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="terminal-interaction-and-automation"> <a href="#terminal-interaction-and-automation" title="Terminal Interaction and Automation">Terminal Interaction and Automation</a> <a href="#terminal-interaction-and-automation" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Terminal Interaction and Automation">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>opencode </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The default command opens the terminal UI.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI reference</a> </span> also documents programmatic commands. Start in the intended repository and confirm the selected agent and model before asking for edits.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>opencode run <span style="color:#e6db74">"Identify this project's test command. Do not modify files."</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Use <code>opencode run</code> for a bounded non-interactive request.</strong> Establish the appropriate permission policy separately. A prompt requesting no changes is useful direction, but it does not enforce filesystem isolation.</p> <p><strong>Choose this workflow when shell composition matters.</strong> A repeatable wrapper should capture the request, exit status, relevant output, and changed files. Keep failure handling explicit. An empty diff and a success message require different interpretation from a verified fix.</p> <h2 id="desktop-setup-and-compatibility"> <a href="#desktop-setup-and-compatibility" title="Desktop Setup and Compatibility">Desktop Setup and Compatibility</a> <a href="#desktop-setup-and-compatibility" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Desktop Setup and Compatibility">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use the official download page for the intended release.</strong> OpenCode’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="download page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/download"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/download" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >download page</a> </span> lists terminal and desktop packages. At this check, the download page advertises v2 terminal packages while the general documentation also contains older installation examples. Record the exact client and backend versions instead of mixing instructions from different release tracks.</p> <p><strong>Evaluate the desktop interaction with a small real task.</strong> Open a project, confirm the server, submit a bounded request, inspect changed files, and ask for a correction. Judge how much effort it takes to understand the agent’s actions. Do not assume a graphical client provides a complete replacement for your editor and debugger.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Desktop trial</th> <th>Expected evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Project selection</strong></td> <td>Agent identifies the intended repository</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Model selection</strong></td> <td>Provider and model match the trial record</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Command execution</strong></td> <td>Required runtime and tests are available</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Change inspection</strong></td> <td>Full patch is easy to locate and review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Restart</strong></td> <td>Intended project and session remain identifiable</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="configuration-and-model-access"> <a href="#configuration-and-model-access" title="Configuration and Model Access">Configuration and Model Access</a> <a href="#configuration-and-model-access" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Configuration and Model Access">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>OpenCode merges configuration from multiple locations.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="configuration reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/config/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/config/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >configuration reference</a> </span> explains precedence and preservation of non-conflicting settings. Compare the effective model, agent, and permissions, not only a single project file.</p> <p><strong>Provider access belongs to the execution setup.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="provider guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >provider guide</a> </span> describes supported services and compatible endpoints. Credentials, endpoint reachability, and model tool support all matter. A server running elsewhere needs its own valid access to the provider and repository.</p> <p><strong>The client does not set your total inference cost.</strong> Compare billed usage under matching models and tasks. Include repeated runs caused by configuration errors. If you use local inference, record system memory, model format, context size, and runtime settings instead of presenting a desktop download as a free replacement for hosted computation.</p> <h2 id="sessions-and-safe-switching"> <a href="#sessions-and-safe-switching" title="Sessions and Safe Switching">Sessions and Safe Switching</a> <a href="#sessions-and-safe-switching" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Sessions and Safe Switching">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Verify continuity rather than assuming it.</strong> Record the active project and session before moving between clients. Check whether the destination connects to the intended server and displays the intended history. If you start a new session, give it a concise handover with the goal, completed work, and remaining checks.</p> <p><strong>Avoid concurrent edits to one checkout.</strong> Two conversations with different plans still share files when they target the same directory. Use separate worktrees or checkouts for independent experiments. Review before integrating their changes.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Handover record </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Goal: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Current branch and working directory: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Files changed: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Checks already completed: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Known failures: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Next approved action: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>This record makes a handover inspectable.</strong> It also helps distinguish an interface issue from a missing instruction or environment mismatch. Keep credentials out of the record.</p> <h2 id="server-access-and-permissions"> <a href="#server-access-and-permissions" title="Server Access and Permissions">Server Access and Permissions</a> <a href="#server-access-and-permissions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Server Access and Permissions">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Treat the agent server as an execution service.</strong> The server documentation describes optional authentication through <code>OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD</code>. Configure access intentionally before connecting across machines. A reachable agent server is not equivalent to a harmless static website.</p> <p><strong>Review tool permissions independently.</strong> OpenCode’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="permission guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >permission guide</a> </span> defines allow, ask, and deny behavior. Apply the same policy during your interface trial. Do not interpret a client with fewer prompts as safer or more capable without checking the effective rules.</p> <p><strong>Start with a harmless policy test.</strong> Ask for a permitted file inspection and a prohibited edit in a disposable project. Verify observed behavior, then proceed to a bounded implementation. This makes the permission assumption testable.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-your-choice"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-your-choice" title="Troubleshooting and Your Choice">Troubleshooting and Your Choice</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-your-choice" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Your Choice">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Symptom</th> <th>First inspection</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Desktop connection failure</strong></td> <td>Selected server and local sidecar status</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Model missing in one client</strong></td> <td>Server version, provider access, and configuration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Different test result</strong></td> <td>Project directory and runtime environment</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Missing conversation</strong></td> <td>Server and session identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Works until a plugin loads</strong></td> <td>Plugin configuration and release compatibility</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Choose the terminal</strong> if scripted requests and shell context make work easier. <strong>Choose desktop</strong> if graphical project navigation improves your supervision. Keep provider and policy decisions separate from this preference.</p> <p><strong>Next steps:</strong> Compare terminal alternatives in the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI roundup"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI roundup</a> </span> . For local inference requirements, read the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode and Strata guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/strata-opencode-local-coding-agent-16gb/"> <a href="/articles/strata-opencode-local-coding-agent-16gb/" rel="follow me" >OpenCode and Strata guide</a> </span> . For graphical alternatives, use the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GUI roundup"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >GUI roundup</a> </span> .</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: OpenCode vs Claude Code: 2026 Coding Agent Comparison
item.description: Compare OpenCode and Claude Code across model choice, local inference, pricing, permissions, project instructions, and daily coding workflows.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>OpenCode</strong> suits developers who want control over model providers, agent configuration, and local inference. <strong>Claude Code</strong> suits developers who want Anthropic’s integrated coding workflow, Claude subscription access, and documented organizational controls. Both work inside real repositories, where useful results depend on tool execution, project instructions, and verification.</p> <p><strong>The agent and the model are separate choices.</strong> Switching from Claude Code with a hosted Claude model to OpenCode with a small local model changes several variables at once. A difference in results does not establish which agent application is better.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Choose OpenCode for provider flexibility</strong>, open-source customization, and experimentation across hosted or local models.</li> <li><strong>Choose Claude Code for a Claude-centered workflow</strong>, especially when your subscription or organization already supports it.</li> <li><strong>Local execution needs qualification.</strong> A terminal application still sends prompts to its configured inference service.</li> <li><strong>Compare completed work</strong>, including review time and failed attempts, rather than token speed alone.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Scope and date:</strong> This comparison checks official documentation and pricing on October 6, 2026. It presents selection advice, not a hands-on performance benchmark.</p> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> A Git repository, working build and test commands, and access to your intended model. Allow 60–90 minutes for an initial comparison after installation. Difficulty is intermediate.</p> <h2 id="feature-comparison"> <a href="#feature-comparison" title="Feature Comparison">Feature Comparison</a> <a href="#feature-comparison" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Feature Comparison">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Area</th> <th>OpenCode</th> <th>Claude Code</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Agent license</strong></td> <td>MIT open source</td> <td>Proprietary terms</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Primary model approach</strong></td> <td>Configurable providers and models</td> <td>First-party Claude workflow</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Interfaces</strong></td> <td>Terminal, desktop, IDE extension</td> <td>Terminal, desktop, editor integrations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Planning</strong></td> <td>Built-in Plan agent</td> <td>Plan permission mode</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Customization</strong></td> <td>Agent prompts, models, tools, permissions</td> <td>Project instructions and permission policies</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Inference billing</strong></td> <td>Selected provider or optional OpenCode service</td> <td>Subscription or configured API provider</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Local-model route</strong></td> <td>Compatible local inference provider</td> <td>Ollama-documented integration</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Licensing differs from model access.</strong> OpenCode’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="MIT license"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/LICENSE"> <a href="https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/LICENSE" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >MIT license</a> </span> covers its agent software. It does not make a hosted model free. Claude Code’s public repository carries <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Anthropic’s license terms"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md"> <a href="https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Anthropic’s license terms</a> </span> , rather than an open-source license.</p> <p><strong>Interface preference deserves a trial.</strong> The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode introduction"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >OpenCode introduction</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Claude Code overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Claude Code overview</a> </span> describe several ways to work. Neither product is limited to terminal chat. Compare how each interface presents edits, interruptions, and the final diff in your normal environment.</p> <h2 id="models-and-local-inference"> <a href="#models-and-local-inference" title="Models and Local Inference">Models and Local Inference</a> <a href="#models-and-local-inference" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Models and Local Inference">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>OpenCode separates provider configuration from the agent interface.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="provider documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >provider documentation</a> </span> covers multiple hosted services and custom compatible endpoints. This is useful when you want to change models without replacing your daily coding interface. Compatibility still depends on the endpoint supporting the model’s tool calls and request format.</p> <p><strong>Claude Code has several official deployment routes.</strong> Anthropic documents Claude subscriptions, its API, and cloud-platform integrations in its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="third-party deployment guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >third-party deployment guide</a> </span> . Those routes address authentication, billing, and infrastructure requirements. They do not make every model behind an arbitrary gateway equivalent to a supported Claude deployment.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama launch claude </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Ollama documents this Claude Code integration</strong> in its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="setup guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code"> <a href="https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >setup guide</a> </span> . A compatible locally served model supplies inference while Claude Code supplies the agent interface. This does not run Claude’s proprietary model weights locally, and Ollama also offers cloud models. Check the selected model and destination before describing a setup as local.</p> <p><strong>Three layers determine the experience:</strong> the agent decides how to use tools, the model produces reasoning and tool requests, and the inference service determines serving behavior. Local and hosted services fit behind either interface when the integration supports them. The illustration below separates these layers without implying identical feature support.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/agent-model-provider-layers.webp", "caption": "Diagram separating the coding agent interface, model selection, and local or hosted inference services", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-07 21:49:43.476002528 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b546.441617237", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-07 21:49:43.476002528 +0000 UTC m=+546.441617237"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/agent-model-provider-layers.webp" alt="Diagram separating the coding agent interface, model selection, and local or hosted inference services"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Evaluate each layer separately when changing your coding setup</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="pricing-and-running-costs"> <a href="#pricing-and-running-costs" title="Pricing and Running Costs">Pricing and Running Costs</a> <a href="#pricing-and-running-costs" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Pricing and Running Costs">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Software price is only one line item.</strong> OpenCode’s client is free to use, while paid inference depends on your provider. Its optional <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Zen service"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Zen service</a> </span> offers curated model access with token pricing. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Go plans"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/go/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/go/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Go plans</a> </span> provide another billing route with defined usage limits.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Route</th> <th>Listed price</th> <th>What to check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>OpenCode client</strong></td> <td>No software subscription required</td> <td>Separate inference charges</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>OpenCode Go</strong></td> <td>$10/month</td> <td>Included models and usage limits</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>OpenCode Go Plus</strong></td> <td>$40/month</td> <td>Higher allowance and applicable limits</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Pro</strong></td> <td>$20/month, monthly billing</td> <td>Included Claude Code usage</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Max</strong></td> <td>From $100/month</td> <td>Selected usage tier and limits</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>API-backed agent</strong></td> <td>Provider token rates</td> <td>Input, output, caching, retries</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Local inference</strong></td> <td>Hardware and operating costs</td> <td>Memory, electricity, maintenance</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Prices are a dated snapshot</strong>, not equivalent compute allocations. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Claude’s pricing page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://claude.com/pricing"> <a href="https://claude.com/pricing" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Claude’s pricing page</a> </span> lists Pro and Max access, with usage limits and taxes separate. OpenCode Go and Claude subscriptions cover different model selections and allowances. A lower monthly price alone does not identify the cheaper route for your workload.</p> <p><strong>Subscription access and API billing are distinct.</strong> Claude Code’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="cost documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >cost documentation</a> </span> explains usage tracking and API costs. Check your active authentication route before a long session. Treat a provider API key as a separate billing decision instead of assuming an existing consumer subscription pays for it.</p> <p><strong>Measure cost per accepted change.</strong> Include unsuccessful attempts, extra prompts, tests, and review time. A cheaper model which repeatedly breaks a migration often costs more developer time than a higher-priced model which produces a correct patch. This is an evaluation criterion, not a measured ranking of these products.</p> <h2 id="planning-and-permissions"> <a href="#planning-and-permissions" title="Planning and Permissions">Planning and Permissions</a> <a href="#planning-and-permissions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Planning and Permissions">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>OpenCode’s built-in agents separate planning from implementation.</strong> Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="agent documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >agent documentation</a> </span> describes Plan and Build, along with configurable specialized agents. Per-agent model and tool settings support experiments such as using different models for exploration and implementation. Record those choices when comparing results.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span style="display:flex;"><span>{ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"permission"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"edit"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"ask"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"bash"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"ask"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>For OpenCode, merge this fragment into <code>opencode.json</code></strong> if you want approval requests for edits and shell commands. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="permission reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >permission reference</a> </span> defines allow, ask, and deny behavior. Check existing rules before adding a fragment, especially in a repository with organization-specific configuration.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span style="display:flex;"><span>{ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"permissions"</span>: { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"defaultMode"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"plan"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>For Claude Code, merge this fragment into <code>.claude/settings.json</code></strong> to start in Plan mode. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="permission documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >permission documentation</a> </span> distinguishes planning, edit acceptance, automated permission decisions, and other modes. Change modes deliberately when ready to implement.</p> <p><strong>These examples serve different purposes.</strong> OpenCode’s fragment requests approval for two tool categories. Claude Code’s fragment starts a planning workflow. Neither snippet establishes an operating-system sandbox or a complete network policy. Test permission behavior with harmless actions before entrusting either agent with sensitive work.</p> <h2 id="share-your-repository-rules"> <a href="#share-your-repository-rules" title="Share Your Repository Rules">Share Your Repository Rules</a> <a href="#share-your-repository-rules" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Share Your Repository Rules">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-markdown" data-lang="markdown"><span style="display:flex;"><span># AGENTS.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Use the repository's documented build and test commands. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Preserve unrelated changes. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Explain failures before changing dependencies. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Review the final diff before committing. </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Shared instructions reduce comparison noise.</strong> Keep build commands, architecture constraints, and acceptance criteria in one canonical file. OpenCode’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="rules documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >rules documentation</a> </span> describes <code>AGENTS.md</code> and a <code>CLAUDE.md</code> fallback. Do not assume every instruction file is automatically combined.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-markdown" data-lang="markdown"><span style="display:flex;"><span>@AGENTS.md </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Place this import in <code>CLAUDE.md</code> when needed.</strong> Claude Code’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="memory documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory"> <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >memory documentation</a> </span> now describes direct <code>AGENTS.md</code> support, starting in version 2.1.277, subject to settings and instruction-file precedence. A project or ancestor <code>CLAUDE.md</code> changes the default selection. The explicit import supports shared rules when <code>CLAUDE.md</code> is present or direct loading is unavailable.</p> <p><strong>Verify loaded instructions in a fresh session.</strong> Ask each agent to identify the repository’s build command and change restrictions before editing. An incorrect answer signals a setup problem.
