item.title: AI Collaboration Across GitHub, Confluence, and Jira
item.description: Publish a fixed retention proposal across Confluence, GitHub, and Jira with version checks and partial-publication recovery.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="return-to-the-ai-collaboration-course"> <a href="#return-to-the-ai-collaboration-course" title=" Return to the AI Collaboration Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the AI Collaboration Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/ai-collaboration-course-start/"> <a href="/ai-collaboration-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Return to the AI Collaboration Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#return-to-the-ai-collaboration-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" Return to the AI Collaboration Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>The contributor freezes PROP-042 before owners approve it.</strong> A Confluence publisher updates requirements, a GitHub maintainer merges implementation, and operations publishes the runbook. Jira records each step. Perform this after permission verification, because the three systems do not form one atomic transaction. Your publication ledger makes incomplete delivery visible.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Approved intent</strong> differs from delivered behavior.</li> <li><strong>Fixed proposal revisions</strong> bind review.</li> <li><strong>Publication ledgers</strong> expose partial completion.</li> <li><strong>Fresh reads</strong> protect against changed bases.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="workplace setup"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/ai-collaboration-confluence-jira-setup/"> <a href="/articles/ai-collaboration-confluence-jira-setup/" rel="follow me" >workplace setup</a> </span> , publisher access, owners, and repository maintainer. <strong>Estimated time:</strong> two hours. <strong>Difficulty:</strong> advanced coordination.</p> <p><strong>Baseline interface:</strong> browser reads, optional approved chat drafting, and human publication. No connector subscription is assumed. Review tenant availability, scopes, provider handling, and identity mapping before adding an integration. Never share an owner’s credential with a contributor.</p> <h2 id="capture-live-sources"> <a href="#capture-live-sources" title="Capture Live Sources">Capture Live Sources</a> <a href="#capture-live-sources" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Capture Live Sources">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Read MAP-01</strong>, then open REQ-17 and RUN-04 by mapped page ID.</li> <li><strong>Open the page menu, Page History</strong>, and capture numeric versions, status, wording, owner, and exceptions.</li> <li><strong>Read the Jira item</strong> and attach a fixed proposal export or GitHub commit. Its key alone does not freeze review evidence.</li> <li><strong>Read approved POL-01</strong> and the protected configuration baseline.</li> <li><strong>Supply only needed synthetic excerpts</strong> to chat, marking them as snapshots and keeping write-capable actions disabled.</li> </ol> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Task: PROP-042, propose only </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Authority: Confluence REQ-17 for intent, GitHub for behavior </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Read: mapped current pages, versions, scope, exceptions </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Proposal: synthetic export retention from 7 to 30 days </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Output: requirement wording, config diff, runbook, ledger </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Evidence: source ID and captured revision for each factual claim </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Unknowns: missing access and absent runtime observations </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Stop: conflict, changed base, or denied access </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Offline packets remain snapshot-based.</strong> The publisher repeats live reads before writing. Access denial blocks publication. An old export is not a substitute for current authorization.</p> <h2 id="freeze-the-proposal"> <a href="#freeze-the-proposal" title="Freeze the Proposal">Freeze the Proposal</a> <a href="#freeze-the-proposal" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Freeze the Proposal">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span style="display:flex;"><span>{ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"proposal_id"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"PROP-042"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"proposal_revision"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"requirement_base_version"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"runbook_base_version"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"policy_version"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"from_days"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">7</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"to_days"</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">30</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"status"</span>: <span style="color:#e6db74">"awaiting-owner-review"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">"publication_order"</span>: [<span style="color:#e6db74">"requirement"</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">"implementation"</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">"runbook"</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">"delivery"</span>] </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Replace illustrative page versions with actual captured versions.</strong> Attach the fixed JSON and proposed wording to Jira. Each owner records role, decision, proposal revision, source versions, and review time. Any substantive edit returns the package to Review.</p> <p><strong>Product reviews intent and scope. Operations reviews cleanup and recovery.</strong> The maintainer reviews the diff. Reactions on mutable chat messages are not revision-bound approvals.</p> <h2 id="publish-and-read-back"> <a href="#publish-and-read-back" title="Publish and Read Back">Publish and Read Back</a> <a href="#publish-and-read-back" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Publish and Read Back">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Move Jira to Publishing</strong> after the publisher verifies both owner reviews and unchanged source bases.</li> <li><strong>Publish REQ-17</strong> with thirty days and a pending-delivery field. Record the resulting version, scope, and exceptions.</li> <li><strong>Open the GitHub implementation PR</strong>, referencing the approved page version. Change configuration to thirty days and attach a non-authoritative requirement snapshot.</li> <li><strong>Merge after repository review</strong> and read <strong><code>main</code></strong> back. Record committed behavior separately from runtime behavior.</li> <li><strong>Publish RUN-04</strong>, read it back by ID, and record its resulting version. Update requirement delivery references through the publisher.</li> <li><strong>Complete Jira</strong> only after all records agree and the final read-back evidence is attached.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Use the local validator for snapshot consistency only.</strong> Copy the pre-change Confluence requirement into the lab’s baseline JSON schema, capture it, and edit the candidate to thirty days. Use an incremented local snapshot revision while separately preserving actual Confluence versions in Jira. The GitHub-first root-source workflow is not a live Confluence validator. Do not present its green status as verification of external authority.</p> <p><strong>Do not deploy deletion in this exercise.</strong> A real service needs deployment evidence, controlled test data, a hold mechanism, and runtime boundary tests. A merge proves repository state, not retention behavior in production.</p> <h2 id="track-partial-publication"> <a href="#track-partial-publication" title="Track Partial Publication">Track Partial Publication</a> <a href="#track-partial-publication" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Track Partial Publication">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Step</th> <th>Initial state</th> <th>Completion evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>REQ-17</strong></td> <td>Pending</td> <td>Resulting page version</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Configuration</strong></td> <td>Pending</td> <td>Merged commit and review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>RUN-04</strong></td> <td>Pending</td> <td>Resulting page version</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Jira closure</strong></td> <td>Pending</td> <td>Final read-back and transition</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Write each result before attempting the next step.</strong> PROP-042 correlates the individual system events. One completed row never means the entire change is complete.</p> <p><strong>Worked failure:</strong> Confluence publishes thirty days, but GitHub denies merge. Keep Jira Blocked and the requirement marked pending delivery. Product chooses forward completion or reviewed restoration to seven days. Do not promote an emergency README copy into requirement authority.</p> <h2 id="handle-concurrent-edits"> <a href="#handle-concurrent-edits" title="Handle Concurrent Edits">Handle Concurrent Edits</a> <a href="#handle-concurrent-edits" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Handle Concurrent Edits">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Browser baseline:</strong> appoint one publisher during the pilot window. Reopen Page History immediately before editing and after publishing. If another writer changes the source, stop, compare, reconcile, and renew approval. Serialized publication is a procedure, not an atomic transaction guarantee.</p> <p><strong>API extension:</strong> Confluence v2 documents <strong><code>GET /wiki/api/v2/pages/{id}?body-format=storage</code></strong> and <strong><code>PUT /wiki/api/v2/pages/{id}</code></strong> with a version object. A reviewed publisher integration compares the current version with the approved base, submits the next version, and reads back. Never refresh a failed version automatically and retry an old body.</p> <p><strong>API success alone is insufficient.</strong> Check resulting content, source ID, scope, and version. This course supplies no write-capable API client. Human browser publication is the executable baseline for non-coders.</p> <h2 id="verify-negative-cases"> <a href="#verify-negative-cases" title="Verify Negative Cases">Verify Negative Cases</a> <a href="#verify-negative-cases" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Negative Cases">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Injection</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Change source after approval</strong></td> <td>Stop and reapprove against new version</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Remove publisher edit access</strong></td> <td>Deny update, retain pending ledger</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Set Jira to sixty days</strong></td> <td>Stop conflict and preserve Confluence authority</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Runbook publication fails</strong></td> <td>Keep delivery incomplete and assign recovery</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Record actual sandbox results</strong> with actor role and revisions before/after. Do not include protected page bodies in denied-user evidence. Expected results are not measured outcomes.</p> <h2 id="assemble-the-review-package"> <a href="#assemble-the-review-package" title="Assemble the Review Package">Assemble the Review Package</a> <a href="#assemble-the-review-package" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Assemble the Review Package">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Freeze content, not only the proposal label.</strong> PROP-042 appears in every system, but a label does not identify the body an owner reviewed. Include the exact requirement wording, implementation diff, runbook wording, source versions, and publication sequence in one fixed package.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Package: PROP-042 revision 1, illustrative </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Intent: synthetic export retention changes from 7 to 30 days </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Exclusions: production data, backups, legal holds </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Requirement amendment: fixed proposed REQ-17 wording </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Implementation: fixed candidate diff and protected base reference </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Runbook amendment: fixed RUN-04 wording and recovery limits </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Review: product and operations decisions for this package </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Delivery: requirement -> implementation -> runbook -> closure </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Stop: changed source, missing review, denied write, failed read-back </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Keep the packet readable for both owners.</strong> Product needs intent and exclusions. Operations needs the operating change and recovery boundary. Both need to understand the period when approved intent and delivered configuration differ. A bare code diff is insufficient for an owner unfamiliar with repository files.</p> <p><strong>Separate the offline snapshot from live publication.</strong> A consistency pass demonstrates agreement among captured records. Immediately before the first write, the publisher rechecks the mapped pages and the maintainer rechecks the protected base. If either changed, the old package stops at Review.</p> <h2 id="walk-through-the-ledger"> <a href="#walk-through-the-ledger" title="Walk Through the Ledger">Walk Through the Ledger</a> <a href="#walk-through-the-ledger" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Walk Through the Ledger">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative state progression:</strong> the table uses teaching revisions, not observations. Fill your actual resulting versions and commits after each sandbox write.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Step</th> <th>State after successful read-back</th> <th>Remaining work</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Owner review complete</strong></td> <td>Approved package, all published values seven</td> <td>All publication steps</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>REQ-17 published</strong></td> <td>Intent thirty, delivery pending</td> <td>Configuration and runbook</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>GitHub merge read back</strong></td> <td>Intent/configuration thirty, runbook seven</td> <td>Runbook and final reconciliation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>RUN-04 published</strong></td> <td>All applicable records thirty</td> <td>Independent final read-back</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Delivery closed</strong></td> <td>Complete ledger with evidence</td> <td>Declared runtime gaps remain</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Pending delivery is a meaningful state.</strong> It avoids describing the old implementation as compliant with new intent while publication is incomplete. Readers need both values during this period, not a single summary claiming “retention is thirty.”</p> <p><strong>Append failed attempts as separate events.</strong> If a runbook write fails, keep the successful requirement and configuration results. Record the attempted runbook action, failure, unchanged version, assigned role, and next action. Do not reset completed rows to Pending and erase the observed sequence.</p> <h2 id="handle-an-uncertain-write"> <a href="#handle-an-uncertain-write" title="Handle an Uncertain Write">Handle an Uncertain Write</a> <a href="#handle-an-uncertain-write" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Handle an Uncertain Write">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A timeout leaves the outcome unknown.</strong> It does not establish success or failure. In the browser baseline, reopen the mapped source and inspect its current content and history before deciding whether to retry.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Pause the next step:</strong> keep delivery incomplete.</li> <li><strong>Read the destination:</strong> compare current wording, version, and scope with the fixed package.</li> <li><strong>Record the observation:</strong> completed, unchanged, conflicting, or inaccessible.</li> <li><strong>Choose the next action:</strong> continue from verified completion, retry an authorized unchanged step, or escalate a conflict.</li> <li><strong>Retain the uncertainty:</strong> keep the failed/unknown attempt alongside the later read-back.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Do not replay the whole sequence blindly.</strong> Repeating an already completed step adds revisions and risks overwriting unrelated edits. Resume from verified state. If source access is unavailable, choose Hold rather than guessing from the old ledger.</p> <h2 id="compare-recovery-decisions"> <a href="#compare-recovery-decisions" title="Compare Recovery Decisions">Compare Recovery Decisions</a> <a href="#compare-recovery-decisions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare Recovery Decisions">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Situation</th> <th>Decision to review</th> <th>Reason</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Requirement changed, merge denied</strong></td> <td>Forward or compensate requirement</td> <td>Intent and behavior differ</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Configuration changed, runbook denied</strong></td> <td>Finish runbook or back out configuration</td> <td>Operating guidance is stale</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Another owner edits scope</strong></td> <td>Return to Review</td> <td>Frozen approval describes another body</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Write outcome unknown</strong></td> <td>Read destination first</td> <td>Retry depends on observed state</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Publisher loses access</strong></td> <td>Hold and request authorized administration</td> <td>Old authorization does not permit new writes</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Choose against the current state and owner decision.</strong> Forward completion needs current approvals and workable controls. Compensation needs review of the restoration against intervening edits. A recovery change is another publication, not a privileged exception to the process.</p> <h2 id="publication-completion-check"> <a href="#publication-completion-check" title="Publication Completion Check">Publication Completion Check</a> <a href="#publication-completion-check" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Publication Completion Check">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Deliver a package an independent reviewer reconciles.</strong> They should find the exact reviewed proposal, its source bases, both role reviews, each write result, final values, and remaining runtime limitations. Ask them to identify the first incomplete step after an interruption.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> the next action comes from fresh sources plus the ledger, not the previous assistant’s confidence. Carry the final mapped references into retrieval tests, where discovery must preserve the same authority distinction.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-recovery"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-recovery" title="Troubleshooting and Recovery">Troubleshooting and Recovery</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-recovery" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Recovery">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Version changed:</strong> compare history and renew review. <strong>Snapshot check passes but wiki differs:</strong> fetch current Confluence sources again. <strong>Done too early:</strong> reopen through the allowed workflow and record missing steps.</p> <p><strong>Recovery:</strong> use Page History comparison and an owner-reviewed restoration or compensating edit. Record the resulting version rather than assuming restoration resets numbering. Revert configuration through a protected PR if product selects backout. Deleted files remain outside the rollback promise.</p> <h2 id="exercise-and-self-check"> <a href="#exercise-and-self-check" title="Exercise and Self-Check">Exercise and Self-Check</a> <a href="#exercise-and-self-check" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Exercise and Self-Check">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Interrupt after REQ-17 publication</strong> and give another publisher only the map and ledger.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> they fetch current sources, confirm frozen approval, and resume only the authorized pending step. Missing evidence returns work to Review.</p> <h2 id="primary-references"> <a href="#primary-references" title="Primary References">Primary References</a> <a href="#primary-references" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Primary References">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>History and restoration:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Confluence technical documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/use-confluence-for-technical-documentation/"> <a href="https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/use-confluence-for-technical-documentation/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Confluence technical documentation</a> </span> .</li> <li><strong>Versioned API operations:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Confluence REST API v2 pages"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-page/"> <a href="https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-page/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Confluence REST API v2 pages</a> </span> .</li> <li><strong>Workflow controls:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Jira advanced workflows"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/configure-advanced-issue-workflows/"> <a href="https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/configure-advanced-issue-workflows/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Jira advanced workflows</a> </span> .</li> <li><strong>Integration security:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="MCP security best practices"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/latest/tutorials/security/security_best_practices"> <a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/latest/tutorials/security/security_best_practices" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >MCP security best practices</a> </span> .</li> </ul> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Continue with <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Map-First Retrieval"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/ai-collaboration-map-first-retrieval/"> <a href="/articles/ai-collaboration-map-first-retrieval/" rel="follow me" >Map-First Retrieval</a> </span> </strong> after completing a reviewed publication run.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: AI Collaboration Capstone: One Change, Both Tracks
item.description: Deliver a synthetic retention change through GitHub-first and Confluence/Jira workflows with failure evidence and independent review.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="return-to-the-ai-collaboration-course"> <a href="#return-to-the-ai-collaboration-course" title=" Return to the AI Collaboration Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the AI Collaboration Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/ai-collaboration-course-start/"> <a href="/ai-collaboration-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Return to the AI Collaboration Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#return-to-the-ai-collaboration-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" Return to the AI Collaboration Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Deliver PROP-042 twice</strong>, through GitHub-first and through GitHub with Confluence/Jira. You contribute, separate owners review, and authorized publishers apply the change. Use isolated synthetic sandboxes after preceding lessons. The capstone tests the complete procedure, including rejection, recovery, and independent handoff, rather than assistant prose quality.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>One shared change</strong> compares both authority models.</li> <li><strong>Negative tests</strong> matter as much as successful delivery.</li> <li><strong>Evidence packages</strong> support independent review.</li> <li><strong>Lab completion</strong> does not authorize production rollout.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> preceding <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="course modules"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/ai-collaboration-course-start/"> <a href="/ai-collaboration-course-start/" rel="follow me" >course modules</a> </span> , approved sandbox access, and separate reviewers. <strong>Estimated time:</strong> three to four hours plus review. <strong>Difficulty:</strong> advanced.</p> <p><strong>Required artifacts:</strong> charter, map, policy, adapters, baseline, manifest, fixed proposal, owner reviews, ledger, recovery record, and handoff. Missing plan-dependent permissions block completion instead of becoming assumed passes.</p> <h2 id="establish-two-baselines"> <a href="#establish-two-baselines" title="Establish Two Baselines">Establish Two Baselines</a> <a href="#establish-two-baselines" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Establish Two Baselines">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Create isolated runs</strong> named GitHub-first and Mixed. Keep revisions and reviews separate.</li> <li><strong>Restore seven-day baseline</strong> through each track’s approved procedure and capture resulting revisions.</li> <li><strong>Verify denial controls</strong> with contributor and excluded-user accounts.</li> <li><strong>Capture current context</strong> and confirm adapter/policy agreement.</li> <li><strong>Declare the scope:</strong> thirty-day synthetic export retention, excluding real data, backups, and legal holds.</li> </ol> <p><strong>PROP-042 is a correlation label, not reusable approval.</strong> Each run needs its own frozen revision and source evidence. Include run IDs in reports.</p> <h2 id="deliver-github-first"> <a href="#deliver-github-first" title="Deliver GitHub-First">Deliver GitHub-First</a> <a href="#deliver-github-first" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Deliver GitHub-First">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Open the Issue and candidate PR</strong> using the GitHub lessons. Change requirement, configuration, proposal, and runbook together. Capture the protected base, run trusted checks, and obtain product and operations reviews at the final commit.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Run: GitHub-first </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Change: synthetic retention 7 -> 30 days </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Requirement: REQ-17 revision 2 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Configuration: retention_days 30 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Runbook: Retention days: 30 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Proposal: base revision 1, from 7, to 30 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Manifest: protected pre-change source hashes </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Review: product and operations at final proposal revision </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Publication: merged commit and read-back </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Limit: no running deletion service exercised </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Fill actual references from the sandbox.</strong> The outline is expected mapping, not completed evidence. The maintainer merges only after review, then independently reads <strong><code>main</code></strong>. Close the Issue after linking the final records.</p> <h2 id="deliver-the-mixed-track"> <a href="#deliver-the-mixed-track" title="Deliver the Mixed Track">Deliver the Mixed Track</a> <a href="#deliver-the-mixed-track" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Deliver the Mixed Track">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Read Confluence versions and freeze the Jira proposal.</strong> Obtain both owner reviews. Publish the requirement with delivery pending, merge configuration, publish the runbook, and read all systems back before Done.</p> <p><strong>Record each publication</strong> with page version, commit, or transition evidence. Repository requirement copies remain snapshots. The local checker does not establish current Confluence authority.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Comparison</th> <th>GitHub-first</th> <th>Mixed workplace</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Requirement</strong></td> <td>Protected repository review</td> <td>Confluence owner-reviewed publication</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Coordination</strong></td> <td>Issue/PR</td> <td>Jira fixed proposal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Publication unit</strong></td> <td>Repository merge</td> <td>Separate page writes and merge</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Freshness</strong></td> <td>Protected commit</td> <td>Page versions plus commit</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Reviewed revert/compensation</td> <td>Ledger-guided compensation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Choose a workflow by ownership needs.</strong> GitHub-first reduces cross-system coordination. The mixed track preserves workplace homes and adds publication/access checks.</p> <h2 id="run-the-failure-matrix"> <a href="#run-the-failure-matrix" title="Run the Failure Matrix">Run the Failure Matrix</a> <a href="#run-the-failure-matrix" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Run the Failure Matrix">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Case</th> <th>Injection</th> <th>Required observed evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Approved change</strong></td> <td>Submit reviewed thirty-day proposal</td> <td>Consistent read-back and review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Stale context</strong></td> <td>Change source after capture</td> <td>Rejection, reconciliation, reapproval</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Unauthorized write</strong></td> <td>Contributor publishes</td> <td>Denial and unchanged revision</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Conflict</strong></td> <td>Jira says sixty, Confluence seven</td> <td>Block and owner reconciliation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Partial publication</strong></td> <td>Interrupt after one write</td> <td>Pending ledger and recovery</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Access denial</strong></td> <td>Remove task read access</td> <td>No protected text or publication</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Approved completion/backout</td> <td>New reviewed revisions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Handoff</strong></td> <td>New session gets map/ledger only</td> <td>Fresh read and correct next action</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Cross-system conflict belongs to Mixed.</strong> In GitHub-first, test an Issue description conflicting with the approved file. Run other applicable cases in both tracks. A local validator failure does not replace live permission evidence.</p> <p><strong>Keep expected and observed outcomes separate.</strong> For each case record run ID, actor role, initial revisions, attempted action, expectation, observation, resulting revisions, and reviewer decision. Redact credentials and account identifiers from shared reports.</p> <h2 id="assess-completion"> <a href="#assess-completion" title="Assess Completion">Assess Completion</a> <a href="#assess-completion" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Assess Completion">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Pass requires observed evidence for every applicable row</strong> and independent acceptance. Reviewers inspect permissions, source freshness, role review, partial publication, and handoff reconstruction as well as consistency logs.</p> <p><strong>Fail immediately</strong> on unauthorized publication, denied text reaching the model, or silent overwrite of a changed base. Keep work Blocked until corrected controls pass a repeat test. Do not average these failures into a favorable score.</p> <p><strong>Measure completed/blocked cases, rejected stale proposals, denied writes, recoveries, and reviewer time.</strong> Proposed outcomes remain expected until observed. The supplied ten unit tests cover consistency, not live tenant security.</p> <h2 id="plan-the-two-runs"> <a href="#plan-the-two-runs" title="Plan the Two Runs">Plan the Two Runs</a> <a href="#plan-the-two-runs" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Plan the Two Runs">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Do not reuse an approval across tracks.</strong> The requested value is the same, but the source homes, captured revisions, permissions, and publishing sequence differ. Give each run its own evidence directory and review packet.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>capstone-evidence/ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> github-first/ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> charter-and-map </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> captured-sources </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> fixed-proposal </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> role-reviews </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> consistency-results </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> permission-results </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> publication-readback </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> recovery-and-handoff </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> mixed/ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> same evidence categories, independently captured </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>These names are an organization example</strong>, not supplied archive files. Store actual evidence privately in the approved sandbox. Shared course submissions should use role labels and redacted references, while reviewers retain access to native records.</p> <p><strong>Assign a test observer before running failures.</strong> The contributor performs the attempted action. The observer records initial state, outcome, and resulting state. A reviewer later determines whether the evidence supports the claim. Disclose role overlap instead of implying independent acceptance.</p> <h2 id="run-failures-in-isolation"> <a href="#run-failures-in-isolation" title="Run Failures in Isolation">Run Failures in Isolation</a> <a href="#run-failures-in-isolation" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Run Failures in Isolation">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Reset to a verified reviewed state between cases.</strong> Injecting source drift, access revocation, and a runbook mismatch together obscures which control rejected the proposal. One failure per run gives the reviewer a traceable reason for the result.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Capture the initial state:</strong> source revisions, configuration, delivery state, and actor role.</li> <li><strong>Apply one synthetic injection:</strong> change one relevant condition through an authorized test route.</li> <li><strong>Attempt the bounded action:</strong> validation, read, publication, or handoff.</li> <li><strong>Record the observation:</strong> actual output and resulting source state.</li> <li><strong>Repair through review:</strong> preserve failure evidence before restoring controls.</li> <li><strong>Repeat the positive case:</strong> confirm the corrected workflow still delivers permitted work.</li> </ol> <p><strong>A planned failure is still a failure observation.</strong> Do not relabel unauthorized publication as a successful test merely because you intended to probe it. The test succeeded at exposing a defect, but the publication boundary failed and requires repair.</p> <h2 id="interpret-a-mixed-result"> <a href="#interpret-a-mixed-result" title="Interpret a Mixed Result">Interpret a Mixed Result</a> <a href="#interpret-a-mixed-result" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Interpret a Mixed Result">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative evidence package:</strong> local consistency passes, product and operations review the fixed package, requirement publication succeeds, and runbook edit access is denied. Configuration has not yet merged. Jira remains Blocked.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Claim</th> <th>Verdict</th> <th>Reason</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Candidate records agree</strong></td> <td>Supported by local check</td> <td>Supplied records passed comparisons</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Owners accepted intent and operations</strong></td> <td>Requires native fixed reviews</td> <td>Role labels alone are insufficient</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Thirty-day delivery completed</strong></td> <td>Unsupported</td> <td>Required publication steps remain pending</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Permission boundary works for every role</strong></td> <td>Unsupported</td> <td>One denied action has limited scope</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery owner should act</strong></td> <td>Supported as next step</td> <td>Partial delivery needs a reviewed decision</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> keep the run incomplete, verify current sources, and request the appropriate owner decision. Do not finish by weakening permissions or describing the snapshot check as live publication evidence.</p> <h2 id="review-with-an-independent-reader"> <a href="#review-with-an-independent-reader" title="Review With an Independent Reader">Review With an Independent Reader</a> <a href="#review-with-an-independent-reader" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Review With an Independent Reader">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Ask the reviewer to reconstruct events</strong>, not merely read your conclusion. They should locate the approved baseline, fixed proposal, owner decisions, resulting revisions, failed attempts, repair, and remaining gaps without your narration.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Reviewer questions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Which source governs retention intent in this track? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Which exact package did each owner review? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Did any source change after review? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>What was published, and what remains pending? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Which denied action was observed under which role? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Did protected text reach an excluded user's context? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Which repair was reviewed and read back? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Does the fresh handoff reconstruct current state independently? </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Score each requirement separately.</strong> Use Supported, Failed, Blocked, or Not run with an evidence reference. Consistency, approval, permissions, recovery, and handoff are separate requirements. A collection of green local tests does not offset a failed live publication boundary.</p> <h2 id="write-a-bounded-decision"> <a href="#write-a-bounded-decision" title="Write a Bounded Decision">Write a Bounded Decision</a> <a href="#write-a-bounded-decision" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Write a Bounded Decision">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A useful closing decision names the next pilot</strong>, not an unrestricted rollout. For example, choose another synthetic export setting with the same roles and direct lookup route, while leaving real data and automated publication out of scope.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Decision element</th> <th>Required detail</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Scope</strong></td> <td>One next change and its explicit exclusions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>Supported cases and unresolved failures</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Controls</strong></td> <td>Platform-enforced and procedural requirements separately</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Owners</strong></td> <td>Accountable role for each remaining gap</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Runtime gap</strong></td> <td>Untested deletion/deployment behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Stop conditions</strong></td> <td>Missing access, changed authority, unauthorized publication</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Completion check:</strong> both run packages survive independent reconstruction, applicable failure cases have observed evidence, and unresolved controls remain visible. If only the GitHub track is complete, report partial course completion rather than assuming the mixed track would behave the same way.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting-and-backout"> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-backout" title="Troubleshooting and Backout">Troubleshooting and Backout</a> <a href="#troubleshooting-and-backout" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting and Backout">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Only happy-path evidence:</strong> rerun denial and interruption tests. <strong>Overlapping roles:</strong> disclose and repeat with separate users. <strong>Missing plan controls:</strong> stop and obtain an approved sandbox.</p> <p><strong>Backout:</strong> restore baseline through reviewed PRs and Confluence edits, revoke temporary integrations, archive Jira evidence, and perform owner-approved synthetic cleanup after evidence retention. Preserve recovery history.</p> <h2 id="create-the-rollout-decision"> <a href="#create-the-rollout-decision" title="Create the Rollout Decision">Create the Rollout Decision</a> <a href="#create-the-rollout-decision" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Rollout Decision">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Decision: another synthetic pilot, blocked, or rejected </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Evidence: both run packages and failure matrix </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Unenforced requirements: procedural controls listed explicitly </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Provider review: input scope and retention handling </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Owner coverage: product, operations, policy, repository, delivery </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Production gaps: runtime tests, secrets, deployment, access review </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Next action: one bounded follow-up with accountable role </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Review date: assigned by pilot owners </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> synthetic success supports another bounded pilot. Production requires separate approval for real data, deployment, provider handling, and runtime behavior. A successful assistant answer is not deployment authorization.</p> <h2 id="primary-references"> <a href="#primary-references" title="Primary References">Primary References</a> <a href="#primary-references" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Primary References">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Repository controls:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Protected branches"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Protected branches</a> </span> .</li> <li><strong>Workplace access:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Confluence permissions"> <meta href="https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/manage-permissions-on-the-page-level/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Confluence permissions</a> </span> .</li> <li><strong>Delivery controls:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Jira permission schemes"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/grant-or-revoke-permissions-in-a-scheme/"> <a <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Return to the <span
